content.text:
Коротко: на `origin/main` внутренних хостов нет совсем, а «тесты» скиллов — это валидатор плюс ручной прогон агентом, результат которого записан в самом SKILL.md. Проверил через `git show origin/main:...`, наш `quest-setup` в сравнение не включал.

## Как тестируются другие скиллы

Автоматических evals или тест-сьютов нет. Проверка идёт на трёх уровнях:

1. **Валидатор и CI.** `.github/scripts/validate_skills.py` запускается в `.github/workflows/validate.yml`. Он проверяет структуру:
   - frontmatter;
   - ссылки и JSON;
   - регистрацию в `skills/README.md` и `AGENTS.md`;
   - совпадение `.cursor/skills` с `skills`;
   - закоммиченные секреты.

   Содержимое скилла он не проверяет.
2. **Секция `## Agent test` в SKILL.md.** Правило №6 в `CONTRIBUTING-skills.md`: «PR must include agent test», то есть точный промпт и однострочный результат. Сейчас такая секция есть в `catalog-design`, `headless-checkout-integration`, `login-setup`, `login-styling` и `webhooks-impl`. Образцовый пример в `catalog-design`:
   - живой прогон на **sandbox-проекте** с датой;
   - что создано, с HTTP-кодами (201, 200);
   - **после прогона всё созданное удалено** (204, проверено, что пусто);
   - шаги, которые выполнить не удалось, честно помечены как blocked и объяснено почему.

   В `login-setup` результат вообще помечен «⏳ Pending live run», и это приняли. Значит, честный статус допустим.
3. **Рецепты и фикстуры.** В `references/testing.md` лежат инструкции, как проверять интеграцию руками (headless-checkout, webhooks-impl). В `webhooks-impl/fixtures/` лежат синтетические payload'ы. `SECURITY.md` прямо требует чистить реальные email, IP и transaction ID.

## Куда кладут адреса

- Только публичные прод-хосты: `developers.xsolla.com` (подавляющее большинство ссылок), `publisher.xsolla.com`, `api.xsolla.com`, `store.xsolla.com`, `login.xsolla.com`, `secure.xsolla.com` и `sandbox-secure.xsolla.com`.
- `srv.local`, `.loc` и `k8s` по всему `origin/main` дают **ноль совпадений**. Слово «staging» встречается только как абстрактное «ваш staging» в `production/SKILL.md`.
- Окружение переключается не через внутренние хосты, а через **sandbox-режим публичного API** (`sandbox: true`, sandbox-проект). Креды передаются только по имени env-переменной (`XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` и т.п.).
- Отдельных конфиг-файлов с base URL нет, публичные URL прописаны прямо в SKILL.md и `references/*.md`.

Контекст политики: README говорит, что репо публичное специально, чтобы партнёры могли читать и аудировать скиллы. `CONTRIBUTING-skills.md` добавляет, что SKILL.md ревьюят как код, который выполняется с кредами пользователя. Финальное ревью и мёрж делает @j.manashti.

## Что это значит для quest-setup

1. **Внутренние stage-хосты (`*.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local`, `*.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local`), пути `adtech/...`, ERC-20 project id и `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` в публичный скилл не кладём.** Это прямо расходится со всеми остальными скиллами. Фактически блокер 1 решается вариантом B (почистить все слои), а C (спросить владельцев) делаем параллельно.
2. **Как чистить:**
   - если у Quests API есть публичный прод-хост, указать его, как делают остальные;
   - если нет, передавать base URL через env-переменную без значения по умолчанию (например `XSOLLA_QUESTS_API_URL`) и писать «спросите у Xsolla».
   Это вопрос к Фариду или владельцам. Stage-детали и заметки по внутренним эндпоинтам перенести во внутренний Confluence или в `adtech`.
3. **`## Agent test` сделать по образцу `catalog-design`:**
   - промпт, дата, что создано и с какими кодами;
   - что удалено после прогона;
   - что заблокировано.

   Без ID квеста, адресов кошельков, tx hash и хостов. Нашу тестовую квест `2965a600...` логично деактивировать: так делают остальные, у них «всё созданное удалено».
4. Web3-часть с суммами честно пометить как частично проверенную, как в `login-setup` с «⏳ Pending». Базовые единицы сейчас работают только из-за бага воркера, контракт этого не гарантирует.

Отдельно: `CONTRIBUTING-skills.md` запрещает сырые `curl`-команды в скиллах. Стоит проверить наши `references` на это до пуша.

Если согласен, следующим шагом (через субагента на Opus, локально, без пуша) пройдусь по всем 7 слоям стека. Составлю список того, что вычистить и на что заменить, и покажу его тебе до любого rebase.

Кстати, Neuronet MCP требует авторизации в настройках коннекторов claude.ai, поэтому поиск шёл обычным grep.

Это многое меняет: для основной части скилла теперь есть публичный хост, как у остальных скиллов. Я сопоставил твой список с тем, что сейчас лежит в `quest-setup` на `QP-2890-verification`.

| Что в скилле сейчас | Публичная замена | Статус |
|---|---|---|
| `qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` (CRUD квестов) | `https://quests-platform.xsolla.com/api/v2/quests` (+ `/accounts`, `/keys`) | ✅ есть |
| `qp-events-collector.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` | `https://quests-platform.xsolla.com/api/v2/events` | ✅ есть, но надо сверить, что скилл шлёт именно на `/api/v2/events` |
| `qp-data.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` (выполнение, метрики, это шаг verification) | в публичном ingress **нет**, catch-all уйдёт в adtech-server | ❌ проблема |
| `web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local` (read-only lookup) | в списке **нет** | ❌ проблема |
| `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT`, `306916` на stage | убрать | внутреннее |
| Ссылки `Source: adtech/...` в `node-subtypes.md` | убрать или переписать как описание поведения | внутреннее |
| thirdweb RPC и zksync testnet explorer | оставить | уже публичные |

Главный вывод: CRUD и события публикуются нормально. А вот verification-слой (qp-data и minting lookup) снаружи сейчас недоступен. Партнёр с этим скиллом просто не сможет проверить выполнение через API. Варианты для этого слоя:
- проверять только по эффекту: статус награды через публичный API, если он там есть, и транзакцию в публичном explorer'е;
- или честно написать «проверка выполнения пока доступна только через Xsolla».

Stage публичный только для `/api/v1/ledger/sessions`. Поэтому stage в публичный скилл не пишем, как и остальные скиллы (они используют прод + sandbox). Наш E2E-прогон описываем в `## Agent test` без хостов: «internal stage run, дата, что прошло, что удалено или деактивировано».

## План (жду твоего ок)

1. **Проверка эндпоинтов.** Сделать неавторизованные GET-запросы (curl) к `quests-platform.xsolla.com`: `/api/v2/quests`, `/api/v2/accounts`, `/api/v2/keys`, `/api/v2/events`. Ожидаю 401/403, а не 404 и не ответ adtech-server. Это подтвердит роутинг. Никаких POST, никакой авторизации.
2. **Инвентаризация (субагент, только чтение).** Пройти все 7 слоёв и составить точный список замен:
   - хосты;
   - `adtech/`-пути;
   - ERC-20 id;
   - заметки про внутренние эндпоинты;
   - сырые `curl`, если есть.

   Плюс указать, в каком слое каждая строка появляется.
3. **Решение по verification.** Показать тебе, как переписать шаги с qp-data и minting (вариант «по эффекту» или «через Xsolla»), и выбрать вместе.
4. **Исправление стека (Opus, локально, без пуша).** Исправить каждый слой там, где строка появилась. В каждом слое прогнать валидатор и проверить зеркало. Rebase безопасен, потому что ничего не запушено, но делаю его только после твоего явного ок на конкретный список.
5. Отдельно в тот же слой можно положить формулировку про суммы web3 (whole tokens по контракту, base units на stage из-за бага), если одобришь.

Открытый вопрос к Фариду или владельцам: есть ли у qp-data или у статуса наград публичный маршрут в планах? От этого зависит пункт 3.

content.text:
Скиллу этот сервис для работы **не нужен**. Квест создаётся через qp-server, награду выплачивает воркер, а воркер сам ходит в minting-service. Агент туда не пишет вообще. В скилле сервис используется только для трёх **read-only предпроверок** перед созданием Web3-награды ([auth-and-environment.md](skills/quest-setup/references/auth-and-environment.md), секция «Minting service»):

| Запрос | Зачем |
|---|---|
| `GET /currency-bindings` | узнать, какие ERC-20 SKU реально привязаны (для `web3_token`) |
| `GET /skus?project=...` | узнать валидные NFT SKU из каталога (для `web3_item`) |
| `GET /wallet/{xsolla_id}` | проверить, есть ли у пользователя кошелёк |

Предпроверки нужны потому, что **qp-server не валидирует Web3-награду** ([rewards.md:52](skills/quest-setup/references/rewards.md:52)). Он примет любой SKU и любую сумму, а ошибка всплывёт только в рантайме: воркер получит 400 от minting-service, когда пользователь уже выполнил квест. Мы на это и наткнулись в E2E. Первые две попытки упали на формате суммы и на привязке SKU. Предпроверки ловят это до активации квеста.

## Почему в публичном скилле этого быть не должно

1. **Партнёру он недоступен.** Хост внутренний, в публичном ingress его нет. Для внешнего агента эти шаги мёртвые.
2. **Там незащищённые write-эндпоинты.** Похоже, что `POST /claim/erc20` на stage работает без авторизации (тот самый инцидент с 1 USDC). Публиковать адрес такого сервиса плохо, даже если он резолвится только внутри сети.
3. **На проде это всё равно не работает.** В том же файле записано: `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` в prod-конфиге воркера пустой. Значит, любая `web3_token`-награда на проде падает с `Web3TokenNotConfigured`. Для публичного скилла, ориентированного на прод, это важнее хоста.

## Что предлагаю

- Убрать хост и секцию «Minting service» из публичного скилла.
- Предпроверки заменить на «SKU и привязку токена берите у Xsolla, кошелёк пользователя должен существовать».
- Web3-награды пометить как «пока недоступно в production» (или «по согласованию с Xsolla»), пока не заполнят `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` на проде.
- Stage-детали (bindings, default catalog `44056`, ERC-20 project `306916`, chain id) перенести во внутреннюю доку.

Спросить у Eljan стоит две вещи: планируется ли Web3 на проде и должен ли claim быть без авторизации. Их можно добавить в черновик сообщения, который я предлагал раньше.

content.text:
`WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` — это настройка воркера квестов (переменная окружения), а не поле квеста. Она говорит minting-сервису, **из какого IGS-проекта брать ERC-20 токен** при выплате награды `web3_token`.

## Как это работает (по коду в `adtech`)

1. Когда квест выдаёт `web3_token`, воркер вызывает `POST /claim/erc20` у minting-сервиса. Тело запроса: адрес кошелька, `sku`, `amount` и `project` ([web3_api.go:188-193](lib/client-sdk/client_sdk/web3_api/web3_api.go:188)).
2. `project` берётся не из квеста, а из этой переменной воркера ([config.go:200-203](qp-worker-generic-quest/internal/config/config.go:200)). Комментарий в коде:
   > the IGS project id the minting service resolves the (project, sku) pair against to pick the ERC-20 contract
3. Адрес токенного контракта воркер вообще не передаёт. Minting-сервис сам ищет по паре `(project, sku)` в своём конфиге `ERC20_TOKENS`, какой это контракт (например USDC). Это та же привязка, что видна в `GET /currency-bindings`.
4. Если переменная пустая, воркер сразу падает с non-retryable ошибкой `Web3TokenNotConfigured` ([issue_reward_action.go:980](qp-worker-generic-quest/internal/temporal/generic_quest/activity/issue_reward_action.go:980)).

## Значения по окружениям

| Окружение | `WEB3_BASE_URL` | `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` |
|---|---|---|
| qp-worker-generic-quest, stage | web3-stage | `306916` |
| qp-worker-generic-quest, **prod** | web3-prod | **пусто** |
| quest-engine, stage | web3-stage | `306916` |
| quest-engine, **prod** | **пусто** | нет |
| dev, local | — | пусто |

Отсюда два практических вывода:

- **Проект один на весь воркер.** Все квесты всех паблишеров платят токенами из проекта `306916`, независимо от `publisher_id` и `project_id` квеста. Паблишер не может выдавать свой собственный токен. Для мультитенантной платформы это похоже на временное решение, стоит уточнить у Eljan.
- **На проде `web3_token` сейчас не работает.** Минтинг-сервис там настроен, а проект не задан, поэтому любая такая награда упадёт. Для `quest-engine` на проде отключён весь Web3 целиком.

Для публичного скилла отсюда следует: убрать упоминание `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` и `306916`. Партнёр этим не управляет, это наша инфраструктурная настройка. Вместо этого написать, что Web3-токен награды пока доступны только по согласованию с Xsolla.

Проверял на локальной ветке `adtech` `QP-2846-principal-home-scope`, а не на свежем main. Если в main конфиги прода уже поменяли, картина может быть другой. Могу сверить с main, если нужно.

content.text:
Да, ты прав. Скилл описывает **контракт**: что агент отправляет в публичный API, что получает обратно и как понять, что всё сработало. Как воркер ходит в minting, какой там проект и какой контракт — это наша внутренняя кухня. Партнёр на неё повлиять не может, а мы можем поменять её в любой момент, и тогда скилл тихо устареет.

Внутренности попали в скилл, потому что мы писали его, отлаживая stage. Каждую найденную там грабли записывали как инструкцию. Для внутреннего runbook это полезно, для публичного скилла это шум и утечка.

Критерий простой: оставляем только то, что агент **видит или может сделать сам** через публичный API.

| Остаётся | Уходит |
|---|---|
| формат награды `web3_token` / `web3_item` в теле квеста | `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT`, `306916`, default catalog `44056` |
| SKU и параметры токена берутся у Xsolla | minting-service, его хост и эндпоинты |
| у пользователя должен быть кошелёк | как воркер резолвит кошелёк и контракт |
| как проверить результат (статус награды и tx hash в результате) | `Source: adtech/...` ссылки на код |

Да, скилл будет работать через project API key. Это часть Фарида, секции про авторизацию я не трогаю.

GET без авторизации — это не про то, как будет работать скилл. Это разовая проверка роутинга перед тем, как вписать хост в скилл (правило «сначала проверить эндпоинт, потом писать конфиг»). Смысл такой:

- **401/403** — запрос дошёл до qp-server, и тот отказал без ключа. Хост и путь правильные.
- **404 или HTML от adtech-server** — путь не маршрутизируется, catch-all забрал запрос, и в скилл такой URL писать нельзя.

Ключ для этой проверки не нужен, и мне лучше с ключами не работать. Если хочешь проверить глубже, с реальным ответом, запусти сам со своим ключом, результат покажешь:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -H "X-REQUEST-APIKEY: $XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY" https://quests-platform.xsolla.com/api/v2/quests
```

Или пропустим пробу совсем и опираемся на terraform ingress и prod Postman env, которые ты уже нашёл. Для публичного URL в скилле этого, по-моему, достаточно. Как лучше?

=================== SKILL.md
   1 ---
   2 name: quest-setup
   3 description: >-
   4   Creates, inspects and edits Xsolla Quest Platform quests conversationally,
   5   submits a quest event, and verifies that the event actually made the quest
   6   execute. Covers the whole quest document: the node graph and its connections,
   7   the seven node subtypes, the condition grammar, activation limits, and all
   8   nine reward types including web3_item and web3_token ERC-20 payouts. Use when
   9   setting up a quest, adding a trigger or a condition, attaching a reward,
  10   editing or activating an existing quest, firing a test event, or working out
  11   why a quest did not fire — including "create a quest", "add a Web3 reward to
  12   my quest", "make a quest that pays USDC", "trigger my quest", "send a quest
  13   event", "why didn't my quest complete", "list my quests", "activate a quest",
  14   "quest platform API".
  15 metadata:
  16   owner: r.aliyev
  17   domain: quests
  18   status: draft
  19 ---
  20 
  21 ## Status
  22 
  23 This skill is a **draft**. The credential lane it targets is not deployed yet;
  24 see Prerequisites.
  25 
  26 ## When to use
  27 
  28 Use this skill when the developer wants to manage quests on the Xsolla Quest
  29 Platform:
  30 
  31 - Create a quest, as a draft first and then activate it
  32 - Add triggers, conditions or reward actions to a quest
  33 - List, view or edit existing quests
  34 - Submit a single quest event to make a quest run
  35 - Check whether an event actually caused a quest to execute
  36 
  37 Out of scope: on-chain finality, wallet balances and Backpack display. This
  38 skill configures a Web3 reward and reports that a quest executed. For a Web3
  39 reward, a completed reward action means the provider returned a transaction
  40 hash for the claim. The skill never states that a token was delivered.
  41 
  42 ## Prerequisites
  43 
  44 Follow [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
  45 for the required credential, request authentication, internal hosts, and scope
  46 confirmation.
  47 
  48 **This credential lane is not accepted yet.** Quest Platform implements it in
  49 QP-2862, inside QP-2858 Phase 3, which depends on Phases 1 and 2. Until it
  50 lands, authenticated qp-server CRUD requests using this Basic lane return 401.
  51 OpenAPI discovery remains available without credentials on stage, so do not
  52 mistake schema discovery for CRUD readiness. If another credential lane is
  53 provided, verify it against the live contract rather than assuming it works.
  54 Say exactly which lane failed, naming the ticket when it is QP-2862, rather than
  55 reporting a generic authentication failure. For qp-data execution read-back, follow
  56 [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
  57 for current access requirements.
  58 
  59 ## Source of truth
  60 
  61 Follow this order. It is the rule the rest of the skill depends on.
  62 
  63 1. **Routes, path parameters, envelope field names and types, and the
  64    top-level `required` list** come from the service's **live OpenAPI
  65    document**. Fetch it once at the start of the session.
  66 2. **Node subtypes, node `parameters`, the condition grammar, the reward
  67    bodies, conditionally required fields, and every enum the document renders
  68    as a bare `string`** come from this skill's `references/`.
  69 3. On conflict: the OpenAPI document wins on shape, `references/` wins on
  70    rules. Rules that only the server's hand-written validator enforces are
  71    marked as such where they appear.
  72 4. If neither source answers the question, **ask the developer**. Do not infer
  73    a field by analogy with another Xsolla API.
  74 
  75 If a host is unreachable, which usually means no corporate network, say so and
  76 offer to continue on `references/` alone, noting that the envelope may have
  77 drifted. Never continue silently.
  78 
  79 ## Reference material
  80 
  81 - [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md) — hosts, credential, scope, and the incoming auth changes
  82 - [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md) — the quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT
  83 - [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md) — the seven accepted node subtypes and their parameters
  84 - [`references/conditions.md`](references/conditions.md) — condition grammar: types, operands, operators, event counting
  85 - [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md) — the nine reward types and their bodies, including web3_token
  86 - [`references/events.md`](references/events.md) — submitting a quest event to qp-events-collector
  87 - [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md) — reading execution results back from qp-data
  88 
  89 ## Flow
  90 
  91 1. **Bring-up.** Fetch the OpenAPI documents. Check the credential is set. List
  92    quests, show the resolved scope, and get confirmation.
  93 2. **Draft.** Create the quest as `inactive` with the four required fields.
  94 3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
  95    required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
  96 4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
  97    there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
  98    nodes, and an acyclic graph. For a Web3 reward, also run the read-only
  99    checks in [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount
 100    units, and the recipient's wallet. Show the activation limits and the
 101    effective repeat behavior before asking for confirmation.
 102 5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
 103    document.
 104 6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
 105    an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit to
 106    qp-events-collector.
 107 7. **Verify.** Read the execution back from qp-data, correlate its `eventId`
 108    with the collector's returned `event_id` as described in
 109    [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md), and report
 110    whether that event made the quest run and which action nodes completed.
 111    If an action `FAILED`, report its `error` verbatim. Do not report a reward
 112    as delivered.
 113 
 114 ## Safety stops
 115 
 116 - Read back and show the resolved scope before the first write, and get
 117   confirmation.
 118 - Before activation, show every externally observable action and get explicit
 119   confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;
 120   `send_http_webhook` sends event data to an external URL;
 121   `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user notification. Do not activate a
 122   `webshop_personalization` node as if it were a working personalization action.
 123 - If `activation_limits` is absent, ask the developer to explicitly choose
 124   unlimited repeat behavior and acknowledge that every qualifying event may run
 125   the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.
 126 - Ask for confirmation before submitting an event.
 127 - After an uncertain event response, such as a timeout, **do not resend** —
 128   neither with the same idempotency key nor with a new one. A timeout is not a
 129   failure. Report "result unknown" and stop.
 130 - After a `FAILED` reward action, do not resend the event. Fix the quest, then
 131   send a new event with a new key only after the developer confirms.
 132 - If a Web3 reward action is stuck in `RUNNING` or failed on a timeout, do not
 133   send another event. The claim has no idempotency key and may already have
 134   paid; see [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
 135 - Never claim a reward was delivered.
 136 
 137 ## Errors
 138 
 139 Branch on the HTTP status only. The API has no stable machine-readable error
 140 codes.
 141 
 142 | Status | What to tell the developer |
 143 |---|---|
 144 | 401 | Missing or invalid credential. For the credential lane described in the reference, name QP-2862. |
 145 | 403 | The key lacks the required `questconfig:*` capability. |
 146 | 404 | "Not found, or no access, or the project is not onboarded to Quest Platform." Never say the quest does not exist. |
 147 | 409 | Conflict. |
 148 | 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. |
 149 | 5xx | Server error. Retry reads only. |
 150 
 151 Two body shapes exist. Middleware failures return `{"error": "..."}`. Handler
 152 failures return RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. On 422 the `errors[]`
 153 array is **not** filled in: per-field messages are flattened into one `detail`
 154 string joined with `"; "`. Those `location: message` pairs may be shown to a
 155 human, never parsed for control flow.
 156 
 157 `ID 0` is a valid merchant ID and a valid project ID. Never treat it as an
 158 absent value.
=================== references/auth-and-environment.md
   1 # Authentication and environment
   2 
   3 Stage OpenAPI and local runtime snapshots were checked on 2026-09-23. The
   4 stage deployment revision is not pinned here, so revalidate before writes.
   5 
   6 This is the **only** file that names the hosts, the header or the credential.
   7 Everywhere else says "an authenticated Quest Platform request". Keep it that
   8 way: the credential lane is being replaced, and this file is the seam.
   9 
  10 ## Services
  11 
  12 Three Quest Platform services, three jobs, plus one read-only Web3 helper.
  13 Sending a request to the wrong one is the most common mistake.
  14 
  15 | Service | Job | Stage host |
  16 |---|---|---|
  17 | qp-server | quest CRUD | `https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` |
  18 | qp-events-collector | event ingestion | `https://qp-events-collector.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` |
  19 | qp-data | read-only execution and metrics | `https://qp-data.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` |
  20 | web3-minting-service | the minting service; this skill uses read-only lookups only | `https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local` |
  21 
  22 All four are internal. They resolve only on the corporate network. There is no
  23 environment variable for them; this table is the source.
  24 
  25 Each service publishes its own OpenAPI document at `/openapi.json`, without a
  26 credential, on stage. qp-server blocks those paths in production.
  27 
  28 ## Minting service
  29 
  30 The Web3 reward provider. Observed on stage 2026-09-23, revalidate: these reads
  31 returned 200 without a credential.
  32 
  33 | Read | Use |
  34 |---|---|
  35 | `GET /currency-bindings` | ERC-20 SKU bindings: `bindings[]` with `projectId`, `sku`, `tokenStandard` |
  36 | `GET /skus?project=<project id>` | NFT catalog of a project: `items[].sku`, paged with `limit` and `offset` |
  37 | `GET /wallet/{xsolla_id}` | 200 with `walletAddress`, or 404 when the user has no wallet |
  38 
  39 Never call `POST /claim`, `POST /claim/erc20` or any other write on it. Only the
  40 worker pays out, and only through an activated quest.
  41 
  42 Worker settings that decide Web3 behavior (observed on stage 2026-09-23,
  43 revalidate):
  44 
  45 - **ERC-20 project**: `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT`, `306916` on stage. It is empty in
  46   the dev, local and prod worker configs, where every `web3_token` reward fails
  47   with `Web3TokenNotConfigured`, non-retryable. The quest's `publisher_id` and
  48   `project_id` do not change it.
  49 - **Default NFT catalog**: the worker sends no project when it lists or claims
  50   `web3_item` SKUs, so the service's default project applies, `44056` on stage.
  51 
  52 For manual checks by a human only: the stage chain is Xsolla ZK Sepolia
  53 testnet, chain id `579029`, explorer
  54 `https://zksync-os-testnet-xsolla.explorer.zksync.dev`, RPC
  55 `https://579029.rpc.thirdweb.com`. This skill does not call them.
  56 
  57 ## Credential
  58 
  59 ```bash
  60 export XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
  61 export XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
  62 ```
  63 
  64 Sent as `Authorization: Basic base64(merchant_id:api_key)`.
  65 
  66 **Not accepted yet for this lane.** On the deployed build, qp-server recognises only
  67 `Authorization: Bearer` and an internal `X-REQUEST-APIKEY`, so a Basic
  68 credential is rejected as if no credential were sent. On the in-flight auth
  69 branch a merchant-key verifier exists but is a stub that always denies.
  70 
  71 The implementation is QP-2862, inside QP-2858 Phase 3, which depends on Phase 1
  72 (QP-2851) and Phase 2 (QP-2852).
  73 
  74 qp-data currently returned the read-only verification response without a
  75 credential on stage. Treat that as an environment snapshot, not a permanent
  76 contract, and recheck before relying on it.
  77 
  78 ## Service preflight
  79 
  80 Do not assume one service's credential works for the others:
  81 
  82 - `qp-server`: OpenAPI discovery is public on stage; CRUD writes require a
  83   verified credential lane. Do not write while only the rejected Basic lane is
  84   available.
  85 - `qp-events-collector`: verify its own live authentication requirement before
  86   submitting an event. A qp-server credential or a successful OpenAPI fetch is
  87   not evidence that event submission is authorized.
  88 - `qp-data`: use only read-only execution queries. Recheck its authentication
  89   response in the current environment before treating a 200 as durable access.
  90 
  91 ## Scope
  92 
  93 Use the scopeless quest routes and let the scope come from the credential.
  94 Before the first write, list quests and show the developer the `account_id`,
  95 `publisher_id` and `project_id` that come back, then ask them to confirm that
  96 is the right place. Do not guess a scope, and do not silently accept whichever
  97 scope the credential happens to carry.
  98 
  99 The account-scoped route family, `/api/v2/accounts/{account_id}/quests`, is
 100 available when the developer names an account explicitly.
 101 
 102 ## Route families this skill does not drive
 103 
 104 They exist on the platform. They are listed so that you neither pretend they
 105 are missing nor wander into them.
 106 
 107 - `/api/v2/quests/{publisher_id}/{id}` — a publisher-scoped update, delete and
 108   get. No create and no list, so it cannot carry the flow. Use it only if a
 109   developer asks for it by name.
 110 - `GET /api/v2/quests/find-quests` and `GET /api/v2/quests/find-quests-triggers`
 111   — internal processing endpoints behind a legacy master-role check, not
 112   authoring.
 113 - `GET /api/v2/quests/personalization/{user_id}` — a personalization read path,
 114   not quest management.
 115 
 116 ## Incoming changes
 117 
 118 These are open and unmerged. Re-read the deployed contract before assuming any
 119 of it; do not implement against the tickets.
 120 
 121 - QP-2851 Phase 1, service identities and machine identity groundwork. Changes
 122   how a service principal's scope is resolved, and can resolve to a workspace
 123   rather than an account.
 124 - QP-2852 Phase 2, a second human issuer, Xsolla Publisher Account.
 125 - QP-2858 Phase 3, Xsolla scope mapping and the publisher machine lane.
 126   QP-2860 may add project-scoped publisher-facing routes, in which case the
 127   scopeless choice above should be revisited.
 128 - QP-2862, the Basic lane this skill targets.
 129 
 130 Phase 3 makes unknown, un-onboarded and unauthorized projects return
 131 byte-identical 404s deliberately, so that the endpoint cannot be used to
 132 enumerate which projects use Quest Platform. Report a 404 accordingly.
=================== references/verification.md
   1 # Verifying that a quest ran
   2 
   3 Stage OpenAPI and local runtime snapshots were checked on 2026-09-23. The
   4 stage deployment revision is not pinned here, so revalidate before writes.
   5 
   6 Read-back lives on **qp-data**, a separate, read-only service. Follow
   7 [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md) for current access
   8 requirements. If read-back is unavailable, report that verification is
   9 unavailable and do not infer execution or reward delivery from event acceptance.
  10 
  11 `GET /api/v1/quest-executions`
  12 
  13 | Query parameter | Use |
  14 |---|---|
  15 | `questId` | the quest you just triggered |
  16 | `userId` | the user the event named |
  17 | `accountId`, `publisherId` | narrow to a scope |
  18 | `status` | filter by execution status |
  19 | `includeNotTriggered` | also show quests that did not fire |
  20 | `latestPerUser` | one row per user |
  21 | `includeEventBody` | include the originating event |
  22 | `page`, `size` | paging |
  23 
  24 ## What comes back
  25 
  26 Each item carries the execution `status`, the originating `eventId` and
  27 `eventName`, the `quest` with the event names it `listensFor`, the `account`,
  28 the `conditionEvals`, and an `actions` array giving **each action node's own
  29 status**.
  30 
  31 ## Correlate the submitted event first
  32 
  33 Save the collector's returned `event_id` with the submitted payload and
  34 `idempotency_key`. Before asserting current completion, require the execution's
  35 `eventId` to equal that `event_id`, for the intended quest, user and scope.
  36 A completed row for the same quest/user may be a historical success while the
  37 new event is pending or failed. Matching quest/user, event name, timestamps or
  38 the latest row alone is not positive event correlation.
  39 
  40 For this lookup, omit `status`, set `includeNotTriggered=true` and
  41 `latestPerUser=false`, and page through results as needed. Compare `eventId`
  42 locally; the query parameters above do not include an event-ID filter. Inspect
  43 the newest state for the matching event and that row's action statuses. If no
  44 matching event is visible, report completion as unverified and retry reads only.
  45 
  46 Use a bounded client-side read policy: at most six reads over at most 60 seconds
  47 with backoff (for example 2, 5, 10, 15, 15 and 15 seconds). This is a safety
  48 guardrail, not a platform SLA. Then stop and report `unverified`; after an
  49 uncertain submission without an `event_id`, keep `result unknown`.
  50 
  51 After an uncertain submission, if no `event_id` was received, keep **"result
  52 unknown"** unless read-only evidence positively identifies the originating
  53 event and its `eventId`. `includeEventBody=true` can expose the event body for
  54 inspection. Use it only when necessary and redact identifiers, emails and
  55 secret-like properties before showing them. An unrelated success is never
  56 sufficient. Do not assume the

  22

  24 see Prerequisites.
  25

  39 reward, a completed reward action means the provider returned a transaction
  40 hash for the claim. The skill never states that a token was delivered.

  60 
  61 Follow this order. It is the rule the rest of the skill depends on.

  63 1. **Routes, path parameters, envelope field names and types, and the

  65    document**. Fetch it once at the start of the session.

  67    bodies, conditionally required fields, and every enum the document renders
  68    as a bare `string`** come from this skill's `references/`.

  70    rules. Rules that only the server's hand-written validator enforces are
  71    marked as such where they appear.

  73    a field by analogy with another Xsolla API.
  74 
  75 If a host is unreachable, which usually means no corporate network, say so and
  76 offer to continue on `references/` alone, noting that the envelope may have
  77 drifted. Never continue silently.
  78 
  79 ## Reference material
  80 
  81 - [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md) — hosts, credential, scope, and the incoming auth changes
  82 - [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md) — the quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT

  90 
  91 1. **Bring-up.** Fetch the OpenAPI documents. Check the credential is set. List
  92    quests, show the resolved scope, and get confirmation.
  93 2. **Draft.** Create the quest as `inactive` with the four required fields.
  94 3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
  95    required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
  96 4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
  97    there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
  98    nodes, and an acyclic graph. For a Web3 reward, also run the read-only
  99    checks in [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount
 100    units, and the recipient's wallet. Show the activation limits and the
 101    effective repeat behavior before asking for confirmation.
 102 5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
 103    document.
 104 6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
 105    an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit to
 106    qp-events-collector.
 107 7. **Verify.** Read the execution back from qp-data, correlate its `eventId`
 108    with the collector's returned `event_id` as described in
 109    [`references/verification.md`](references/verification.md), and report
 110    whether that event made the quest run and which action nodes completed.
 111    If an action `FAILED`, report its `error` verbatim. Do not report a reward
 112    as delivered.
 113 
 114 ## Safety stops
 115 
 116 - Read back and show the resolved scope before the first write, and get
 117   confirmation.
 118 - Before activation, show every externally observable action and get explicit
 119   confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;
 120   `send_http_webhook` sends event data to an external URL;
 121   `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user notification. Do not activate a
 122   `webshop_personalization` node as if it were a working personalization action.
 123 - If `activation_limits` is absent, ask the developer to explicitly choose
 124   unlimited repeat behavior and acknowledge that every qualifying event may run
 125   the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.
 126 - Ask for confirmation before submitting an event.
 127 - After an uncertain event response, such as a timeout, **do not resend** —
 128   neither with the same idempotency key nor with a new one. A timeout is not a
 129   failure. Report "result unknown" and stop.
 130 - After a `FAILED` reward action, do not resend the event. Fix the quest, then
 131   send a new event with a new key only after the developer confirms.
 132 - If a Web3 reward action is stuck in `RUNNING` or failed on a timeout, do not
 133   send another event. The claim has no idempotency key and may already have
 134   paid; see [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
 135 - Never claim a reward was delivered.
 136 
 137 ## Errors
 138 
 139 Branch on the HTTP status only. The API has no stable machine-readable error
 140 codes.
 141 
 142 | Status | What to tell the developer |
 143 |---|---|
 144 | 401 | Missing or invalid credential. For the credential lane described in the reference, name QP-2862. |
 145 | 403 | The key lacks the required `questconfig:*` capability. |
 146 | 404 | "Not found, or no access, or the project is not onboarded to Quest Platform." Never say the quest does not exist. |
 147 | 409 | Conflict. |
 148 | 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. |
 149 | 5xx | Server error. Retry reads only. |
 150 
 151 Two body shapes exist. Middleware failures return `{"error": "..."}`. Handler
 152 failures return RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. On 422 the `errors[]`
 153 array is **not** filled in: per-field messages are flattened into one `detail`
 154 string joined with `"; "`. Those `location: message` pairs may be shown to a
 155 human, never parsed for control flow.
 156 
 157 `ID 0` is a valid merchant ID and a valid project ID. Never treat it as an
 158 absent value.

  37 form. `name`, `image_url` and `model_3d_url` are supported with the single-item
  38 form; obtain real catalog values from the developer. An empty body can mean a
  39 runtime-selected item, so do not treat acceptance as proof of a particular SKU.

  41 ## Web3 recipient
  42 
  43 Both `web3_item` and `web3_token` pay to the wallet of the event's user. The
  44 event's `user_ids` must include an `xsolla_id`, and that user must already have
  45 a wallet. Before activation and again before submitting an event, read the
  46 minting service's wallet lookup for that `xsolla_id`
  47 ([`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md)). A 404 means no wallet:
  48 the reward fails with `RecipientNotFound`, non-retryable. Report it and stop.

  51 
  52 qp-server does not check a Web3 body against the minting service. It accepts
  53 `0.01` and `10000`, and a SKU that is not bound, on create, `PUT` and
  54 activation alike. Those mistakes appear only at payout time, as a `FAILED`
  55 `issue_reward` action whose `error` names the cause; see
  56 [`verification.md`](verification.md). Run the checks below before activation.
  57 
  58 ## web3_item
  59 
  60 An NFT from the minting service's catalog.
  61 
  62 SKUs come from the IGS publisher catalog. The minting service lists a
  63 project's catalog with its read-only SKU lookup
  64 ([`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md)). For `web3_item` the
  65 worker sends no project to the minting service, so only SKUs from the service's default catalog
  66 are usable through a quest today (observed on stage 2026-09-23, revalidate).
  67 Read that catalog and use a real `items[].sku`; do not invent one.
  68 
  69 Omitting `item_sku` makes the worker list the default catalog and pick one item
  70 at random. Tell the developer before choosing that.
  71 
  72 ## web3_token
  73 
  74 An ERC-20 payout, for example USDC.
  75 
  76 ```json
  77 {
  78   "type": "web3_token",
  79   "purpose": "quest_completion",
  80   "body": {"item_sku": "GM26", "amount": 10000}
  81 }
  82 ```
  83

  85 fixture. On stage, `GM26` with `10000` paid 0.01 USDC.

  87 **`amount` is a positive integer in the token's base units** (observed on stage
  88 2026-09-23, revalidate). The worker passes `body.amount` to the minting service
  89 verbatim. The service rejects a decimal with a 400, `amount must be a positive
  90 integer (digits only, no sign or decimal point)`. USDC has 6 decimals, so
  91 `1000000` is 1.00 USDC and `10000` is 0.01 USDC. Whether `amount` is meant to
  92 be whole tokens or base units is pending confirmation from the Web3 owner. Get
  93 the token's decimals from the developer or the owner, never guess them, and
  94 show both the token amount and the base-unit integer before activation.

  96 **`item_sku` must be a current ERC-20 binding of the worker's ERC-20 project.**
  97 Read the minting service's currency bindings
  98 ([`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md)) and pick a binding with
  99 `tokenStandard: erc20` whose `projectId` equals the worker's ERC-20 project.

 101 memory. An unbound SKU fails at payout with a 400, `no ERC-20 token is
 102 configured for project <id> / sku <sku>`.
 103 
 104 **The ERC-20 project comes from the worker's environment**, not from the
 105 quest's `publisher_id` or `project_id`. Where it is not configured, every
 106 `web3_token` reward fails with `Web3TokenNotConfigured`, non-retryable.
 107 Currently only stage has it; see
 108 [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md). Do not offer this reward
 109 in another environment without owner confirmation.
 110 
 111 **What a `COMPLETED` reward action means.** The worker calls the claim
 112 synchronously and treats a missing transaction hash as a non-retryable error.
 113 So a `COMPLETED` `issue_reward` means the minting service returned a
 114 transaction hash: the claim was submitted. On-chain finality, the wallet
 115 balance and Backpack or Rewards display are outside this skill's evidence.
 116 Never claim that the token reached the wallet. The hash is recorded by the
 117 worker, not in qp-data: its logs carry a `tx_hash` field on the
 118 `claim_web3_token` success line, and its ledger keeps the hash only inside the
 119 reward node's result text (`Transaction hash: <hash>`), not as a separate field. The minting service's minted-instances list is not a per-claim log;
 120 a new ERC-20 claim did not appear there. A human can check the hash on the
 121 chain explorer named in [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md).
 122 
 123 **Duplicate payout risk.** The claim carries no idempotency key. The reward
 124 activity has a 2-minute timeout and up to 3 attempts. HTTP errors from the
 125 claim are non-retryable, but an activity timeout or a worker crash after the
 126 provider paid can run the claim again. If an execution is stuck in `RUNNING`,
 127 or its reward action failed on a timeout, do not resend the event. Ask a human
 128 to check the worker logs or the chain first.
 129 
 130 Attaching this reward to a quest that you then activate means real payouts. Ask
 131 for explicit confirmation before activating.

   1 # Events
   2 
   3 Stage OpenAPI and local runtime snapshots were checked on 2026-09-23. The
   4 stage deployment revision is not pinned here, so revalidate before writes.
   5 
   6 Events go to **qp-events-collector**, not to qp-server. Sending an event to
   7 qp-server produces a 404 that looks like a missing quest.
   8 
   9 `POST /api/v2/events`
  10 
  11 ## Payload
  12 
  13 ```json
  14 {
  15   "idempotency_key": "<uuid>",
  16   "name": "<event_name from the trigger>",
  17   "client_timestamp": "2026-09-22T10:30:00Z",
  18   "user_ids": [{"identifier_type": "xsolla_id", "value": "<uuid>"}],
  19   "quest_id": "<uuid>",
  20   "scope": "private",
  21   "publisher": {"publisher_id": "<string>", "project_id": "<string>"},
  22   "properties": {"any": "string values only"}
  23 }
  24 ```
  25 
  26 | Field | Required | Rules |
  27 |---|---|---|
  28 | `idempotency_key` | yes | a valid, non-zero UUID. Any version is accepted despite the schema hinting at v4 |
  29 | `name` | yes | must match the `event_name` on the quest's `dynamic_event` trigger |
  30 | `client_timestamp` | yes | RFC3339 |
  31 | `user_ids` | yes | at least one entry |
  32 | `quest_id` | no | a valid UUID when present |
  33 | `scope` | no | `global`, `private`, `within_project`, `within_quest`, `within_publisher`. Defaults to `private`. The published schema shows a bare string and the older struct hint lists only three values; the server accepts all five |
  34 | `publisher` | no | if the object is present and non-empty, `publisher.publisher_id` is required |
  35 | `properties` | no | string values only |
  36 
  37 `user_ids[].identifier_type` is `xsolla_id`, `gamer_id`, `guest_id` or `email`.
  38 An `xsolla_id` value must parse as a UUID; an `email` value must contain `@`;
  39 `gamer_id` and `guest_id` need only be non-empty.
  40 
  41 A quest with a `web3_item` or `web3_token` reward needs an `xsolla_id` entry
  42 whose user already has a wallet. Check it before submitting; see
  43 [`rewards.md`](rewards.md).
  44 
  45 The account is **not** in the body. It comes from the credential.
  46 
  47 A 200 returns `{"idempotency_key": "...", "event_id": "<uuid>"}`.
  48 
  49 ## Idempotency
  50 
  51 There are two separate mechanisms and they are easy to confuse:
  52 
  53 - the body field `idempotency_key`, which the platform uses as the message key
  54 - a generic HTTP `X-Idempotency-Key` header handled by middleware, which must
  55   be exactly 36 characters
  56 
  57 Use the body field. Generate a fresh UUID per event.
  58 
  59 ## After an uncertain response
  60 
  61 If the request times out or the outcome is otherwise unknown, **stop**. Do not
  62 resend, not with the same key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
  63 failure: the event may have been accepted and the quest may already be paying
  64 out. Report "result unknown", and use the execution read-back to find out what
  65 really happened.
=================== references/node-subtypes.md
   1 # Node subtypes
   2 
   3 Stage OpenAPI and local runtime snapshots were checked on 2026-09-22. The
   4 stage deployment revision is not pinned here, so revalidate before writes.
   5 
   6 The OpenAPI document types `subtype` as a bare `string`. The real list lives in
   7 the server's validator, and it is shorter than the constants suggest.
   8 Node `parameters` are raw JSON in OpenAPI; use the source-backed rules below
   9 for their shapes and validation, following the skill's source-of-truth order.
  10 
  11 ## Accepted
  12 
  13 | `subtype` | Used with `type` | `parameters` |
  14 |---|---|---|
  15 | `date_and_time` | trigger | accepted without parameter validation; scheduling is not implemented |
  16 | `dynamic_event` | trigger | `{"event_name": "<non-empty string>"}` |
  17 | `custom_attributes_check` | condition | see `conditions.md` |
  18 | `issue_reward` | action | see `rewards.md` |
  19 | `send_xsolla_app_notification` | action | `topic`, `notification_type`, `title`, `message`; optional `data`, see below |
  20 | `send_http_webhook` | action | `url`, see below |
  21 | `webshop_personalization` | action | configuration is accepted, but the current worker maps it to `SkipExecution`; see below |
  22 
  23 ## Action parameters
  24 
  25 These rules are enforced by the server's hand-written validators, registered
  26 in `adtech/qp-server/internal/http/validation/quest_config.go`. Each of these
  27 three actions requires `parameters` that decode into its model and pass
  28 validation; OpenAPI does not supply this contract. Ask the developer for actual
  29 values, including the notification topic, webhook URL and personalization IDs.
  30 
  31 Configuration acceptance is not runtime support. The current worker maps
  32 `webshop_personalization` to `SkipExecution`; it must not be presented as a
  33 working personalization effect without an owner-approved stage fixture and a
  34 deployed implementation check.
  35 
  36 ### send_http_webhook
  37 
  38 ```json
  39 {"url": "<developer-supplied HTTP or HTTPS URL>"}
  40 ```
  41 
  42 `url` is the only modeled parameter. It must be a non-empty string, parse with
  43 Go's `url.ParseRequestURI`, use the `http` or `https` scheme, and have a
  44 non-empty host. The model supplies no method, headers or body parameters.
  45 When the quest executes, the worker sends the full event JSON by HTTP POST to
  46 this URL. Require an approved stage endpoint and explicit activation approval;
  47 never treat an arbitrary developer-supplied URL as a harmless placeholder.
  48 
  49 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/http_webhook.go`.
  50 
  51 ### send_xsolla_app_notification
  52 
  53 ```json
  54 {
  55   "topic": "<developer-supplied topic>",
  56   "notification_type": "<developer-supplied notification type>",
  57   "title": "<developer-supplied title>",
  58   "message": "<developer-supplied message>",
  59   "data": {}
  60 }
  61 ```
  62 
  63 `topic`, `notification_type`, `title` and `message` are required non-empty
  64 strings. `topic` is required by `Validate()` despite its `omitempty` JSON tag.
  65 The validator does not constrain these strings to an enum or check a topic's
  66 existence. `data` is optional, a JSON object with string keys and arbitrary
  67 JSON values; it has no additional validation. Do not invent a topic or
  68 notification-type value.
  69 
  70 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/xsolla_app_notification.go`.
  71 
  72 ### webshop_personalization
  73 
  74 ```json
  75 {"items": [{"id": "<developer-supplied item ID>"}]}
  76 ```
  77 
  78 `items` must be a non-empty array. Each item is modeled as an object with a
  79 string `id`. The validator checks only the array length; it does not require
  80 each `id` to be present or non-empty, check its format, or verify that the item
  81 exists. Obtain real IDs from the developer rather than treating acceptance as
  82 proof of a valid item.
  83 
  84 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/webshop_personalization.go`.
  85 
  86 ## Accepted for configuration, not a working runtime action
  87 
  88 `webshop_personalization` is accepted by the configuration validator, but the
  89 current worker routes it to `SkipExecution`. Do not use API acceptance or a
  90 `COMPLETED` execution row as evidence that personalization occurred.
  91 
  92 ## Rejected, despite existing
  93 
  94 `event_check` is declared as a constant in the platform's models but is **not**
  95 in the accepted list. A node using it fails validation. Do not offer it, and if
  96 a developer asks for it, say it is not accepted by the API.
  97 
  98 ## Choosing a trigger
  99 
 100 For a quest that should run when something happens, use `dynamic_event` and set
 101 `event_name` to the name the event will carry. That name is what ties the quest
 102 to the event submitted later; see `events.md`.
 103 
 104 `date_and_time` is accepted by the API and its parameters are not validated
 105 on write, but **runtime scheduling is not implemented**. The current
 106 `DateAndTimeTrigger` is a TODO stub (QP-591): it logs and returns success when
 107 invoked, without reading schedule parameters or scheduling an execution.
 108 API acceptance or a successful stub invocation is not evidence that a schedule
 109 will run. Do not recommend it as a working scheduler or invent schedule fields.
 110 For a scheduling request, explain this limitation before configuring a quest.
 111 
 112 Source: local `adtech/qp-worker-generic-quest/internal/temporal/generic_quest/activity/trigger.go`,
 113 checked on 2026-09-22. Revalidate the deployed worker before claiming runtime behavior.

  62 resend, not with the same key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
  63 failure: the event may have been accepted and the quest may already be paying
  64 out. Report "result unknown", and use the execution read-back to find out what
  65 really happened.
=================== references/node-subtypes.md
   1 # Node subtypes
   2 
   3 Stage OpenAPI and local runtime snapshots were checked on 2026-09-22. The
   4 stage deployment revision is not pinned here, so revalidate before writes.
   5 
   6 The OpenAPI document types `subtype` as a bare `string`. The real list lives in
   7 the server's validator, and it is shorter than the constants suggest.
   8 Node `parameters` are raw JSON in OpenAPI; use the source-backed rules below
   9 for their shapes and validation, following the skill's source-of-truth order.
  10 
  11 ## Accepted
  12 
  13 | `subtype` | Used with `type` | `parameters` |
  14 |---|---|---|
  15 | `date_and_time` | trigger | accepted without parameter validation; scheduling is not implemented |
  16 | `dynamic_event` | trigger | `{"event_name": "<non-empty string>"}` |
  17 | `custom_attributes_check` | condition | see `conditions.md` |
  18 | `issue_reward` | action | see `rewards.md` |
  19 | `send_xsolla_app_notification` | action | `topic`, `notification_type`, `title`, `message`; optional `data`, see below |
  20 | `send_http_webhook` | action | `url`, see below |
  21 | `webshop_personalization` | action | configuration is accepted, but the current worker maps it to `SkipExecution`; see below |
  22 
  23 ## Action parameters
  24 
  25 These rules are enforced by the server's hand-written validators, registered
  26 in `adtech/qp-server/internal/http/validation/quest_config.go`. Each of these
  27 three actions requires `parameters` that decode into its model and pass
  28 validation; OpenAPI does not supply this contract. Ask the developer for actual
  29 values, including the notification topic, webhook URL and personalization IDs.
  30 
  31 Configuration acceptance is not runtime support. The current worker maps
  32 `webshop_personalization` to `SkipExecution`; it must not be presented as a
  33 working personalization effect without an owner-approved stage fixture and a
  34 deployed implementation check.
  35 
  36 ### send_http_webhook
  37 
  38 ```json
  39 {"url": "<developer-supplied HTTP or HTTPS URL>"}
  40 ```
  41 
  42 `url` is the only modeled parameter. It must be a non-empty string, parse with
  43 Go's `url.ParseRequestURI`, use the `http` or `https` scheme, and have a
  44 non-empty host. The model supplies no method, headers or body parameters.
  45 When the quest executes, the worker sends the full event JSON by HTTP POST to
  46 this URL. Require an approved stage endpoint and explicit activation approval;
  47 never treat an arbitrary developer-supplied URL as a harmless placeholder.
  48 
  49 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/http_webhook.go`.
  50 
  51 ### send_xsolla_app_notification
  52 
  53 ```json
  54 {
  55   "topic": "<developer-supplied topic>",
  56   "notification_type": "<developer-supplied notification type>",
  57   "title": "<developer-supplied title>",
  58   "message": "<developer-supplied message>",
  59   "data": {}
  60 }
  61 ```
  62 
  63 `topic`, `notification_type`, `title` and `message` are required non-empty
  64 strings. `topic` is required by `Validate()` despite its `omitempty` JSON tag.
  65 The validator does not constrain these strings to an enum or check a topic's
  66 existence. `data` is optional, a JSON object with string keys and arbitrary
  67 JSON values; it has no additional validation. Do not invent a topic or
  68 notification-type value.
  69 
  70 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/xsolla_app_notification.go`.
  71 
  72 ### webshop_personalization
  73 
  74 ```json
  75 {"items": [{"id": "<developer-supplied item ID>"}]}
  76 ```
  77 
  78 `items` must be a non-empty array. Each item is modeled as an object with a
  79 string `id`. The validator checks only the array length; it does not require
  80 each `id` to be present or non-empty, check its format, or verify that the item
  81 exists. Obtain real IDs from the developer rather than treating acceptance as
  82 proof of a valid item.
  83 
  84 Source: `adtech/lib/models/generic_quest/webshop_personalization.go`.
  85 
  86 ## Accepted for configuration, not a working runtime action
  87 
  88 `webshop_personalization` is accepted by the configuration validator, but the
  89 current worker routes it to `SkipExecution`. Do not use API acceptance or a
  90 `COMPLETED` execution row as evidence that personalization occurred.
  91 
  92 ## Rejected, despite existing
  93 
  94 `event_check` is declared as a constant in the platform's models but is **not**
  95 in the accepted list. A node using it fails validation. Do not offer it, and if
  96 a developer asks for it, say it is not accepted by the API.
  97 
  98 ## Choosing a trigger
  99 
 100 For a quest that should run when something happens, use `dynamic_event` and set
 101 `event_name` to the name the event will carry. That name is what ties the quest
 102 to the event submitted later; see `events.md`.
 103

 106 `DateAndTimeTrigger` is a TODO stub (QP-591): it logs and returns success when
 107 invoked, without reading schedule parameters or scheduling an execution.
 108 API acceptance or a successful stub invocation is not evidence that a schedule
 109 will run. Do not recommend it as a working scheduler or invent schedule fields.
 110 For a scheduling request, explain this limitation before configuring a quest.

Инвентаризацию закончил. Я прочитал все 8 файлов на `6199a82`. Цепочка не менялась, зеркало совпадает. Ничего не правил.

## Что нашлось

**Уходит однозначно:**
- `auth-and-environment.md`: таблица «Services» с 4 хостами `*.srv.local`, «corporate network», вся секция «Minting service» (эндпоинты, `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT`, `306916`, `44056`, chain id).
- `rewards.md`: предпроверки через minting (кошелёк, `/skus`, `/currency-bindings`), «на stage `GM26` с `10000` = 0.01 USDC», про base units и stage-баг, где воркер хранит tx hash (логи, ledger).
- `node-subtypes.md`: 5 ссылок `Source: adtech/...`, `QP-591`.
- Шапка «Stage OpenAPI ... checked on 2026-09-2x, revalidate» во всех 7 references и «observed on stage» в тексте.
- `SKILL.md`: «usually means no corporate network», «internal hosts».
- **Сообщения коммитов** тоже станут публичными. В `4f50a83` есть minting service, `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` и «stage only».

**Оставляю, но переформулирую как наблюдаемое поведение без механики:** `date_and_time` не планирует запуск, `webshop_personalization` ничего не делает, claim не идемпотентен (застрял в `RUNNING` — не переотправлять), qp-server не проверяет Web3-тело.

## Нужны твои решения (3 вопроса)

1. **Auth-секции.** Трогать их нельзя, это зона Фарида. Но в них тоже лежит внутреннее: `internal X-REQUEST-APIKEY`, «on the in-flight auth branch ... stub that always denies», «qp-data отвечает без креденшала на stage» и 8 Jira-ключей QP-28xx. Ни в одном другом скилле на main Jira-ключей нет. Варианты: я чищу только внутренние детали и не меняю смысл, или оставляем Фариду, но тогда эти строки уедут в публичное репо.
2. **qp-data (весь слой verification).** Наружу он не маршрутизируется. Без него скилл не может проверить, что квест выполнился. Варианты:
   - (a) описать контракт `GET /api/v1/quest-executions` без хоста, с пометкой «доступ через Xsolla»;
   - (b) пока не публиковать слой verification, стек из 6 PR;
   - (c) сначала спросить владельцев.
3. **Правило «Source of truth: live OpenAPI».** В том же файле написано, что на проде qp-server `/openapi.json` блокирует. Значит, у внешнего агента пункт 1 правила не сработает. Нужно понять, есть ли публичная дока Quests API (developers.xsolla.com?) и можно ли сослаться на неё. Могу проверить, не отправляя данных наружу.

## Как переписать историю

Слой verification переписывает все файлы (+410 строк), поэтому точечные fixup'ы в нижних слоях дадут конфликты при каждом rebase. Предлагаю по одному чистому коммиту на слой. content.text:
Да, эндпоинт есть, но партнёру он сейчас недоступен.

**Что есть:**
- Сервис `qp-data` лежит в `adtech` на `origin/dev` (добавлен 2026-08-18). Роут `/quest-executions` объявлен в [router.go](qp-data/internal/http/router.go:44).
- На stage он задеплоен. Мы сами получили оттуда 200 во время E2E. Комментарий в [qpdata_client.go:84](qp-admin/internal/http/admin/qpdata_client.go:84) это подтверждает: на stage пока есть только `/api/v1/quest-executions`, а `/quests` ещё нет.

**Почему партнёру он не подходит:**
- **Авторизация временная и не наша.** По комментарию в конфиге это «temporary overlay auth»: заголовок `X-QP-Api-Key`, два ключа, admin и overlay, оба инжектятся как секреты.
  - На stage `AUTH_ENABLED: 'false'`, поэтому мы и получили 200 без креденшала.
  - На prod `AUTH_ENABLED: 'true'`, а overlay-ключ ограничен белым списком из 6 конкретных quest ID.

  Project API key там не поддерживается вообще.
- **Наружу не маршрутизируется.** В твоём списке ingress qp-data нет. В qp-admin упоминается «external `/quests/data/v1/X` maps to internal `/api/v1/X`». Похоже, внешний путь где-то задуман в доке, но в terraform-роутинге, который ты нашёл, его нет.
- Задеплоен ли qp-data на prod вообще, я не проверял. Видел только, что prod-конфиг существует.

**Вывод для скилла:** слой verification в публичной версии сейчас не работает. Нет публичного хоста, нет авторизации по project API key, а prod-доступ ограничен вайтлистом. Поэтому я бы выбрал вариант (b): публикуем стек из 6 PR, verification пока держим локально. Выпустим его, когда qp-data получит внешний маршрут и нормальную авторизацию.

Тогда скилл после отправки события честно пишет «событие принято, `event_id` такой-то; выполнение квеста этим скиллом пока не проверяется». Владельцам qp-data (или Фариду) стоит задать вопрос: есть ли план на `/quests/data/v1` снаружи и на project API key.

Идём с (b)? И остаются ещё два вопроса: auth-секции и live OpenAPI на проде.

content.text:
Это шаг 7 в Flow скилла, **Verify**. Эндпоинт нужен не для информации о самом квесте (её отдаёт qp-server), а для ответа на вопрос: **«событие, которое я отправил, реально запустило квест, и награда выдалась?»**

Зачем мы это вообще заложили:

1. **Приём события ничего не гарантирует.** Collector возвращает 200 и `event_id`, даже если квест потом не сработал: имя события не совпало с триггером, квест `inactive`, лимит активаций исчерпан, условие не прошло.
2. **Ошибки наград видны только в рантайме.** qp-server принимает любое Web3-тело, а падает уже выплата: неправильная сумма, непривязанный SKU, нет кошелька. Мы сами так упали два раза в E2E и узнали об этом только из статуса `FAILED` у action-ноды.
3. **Это обещано в описании скилла:** «verifies that the event actually made the quest execute» и триггер «why didn't my quest complete». Без read-back агент на такой вопрос может ответить только «событие принято, дальше не знаю».

Отсюда закономерный вопрос: нужно ли это в первой публичной версии? Если основная задача скилла — **настроить квест** (создать, заполнить, активировать, отправить тестовое событие), то verification можно честно вынести за рамки:
- убрать из description обещание проверки и триггер «why didn't my quest complete»;
- после отправки события скилл говорит: «событие принято, `event_id` такой-то; результат выполнения смотрите в Publisher Account / у Xsolla»;
- слой verification вернём, когда появится публичный эндпоинт (`/api/v1/quests/info` через ingress).

Для публикации сейчас я бы так и сделал. Скилл получается честным и не зависит от внутренних сервисов. Согласен?

entries.description: Get a Confluence page or blog post by ID, including body content.

pageId.description: Page or blog post ID, or a Confluence tiny link ID (the encoded part from /wiki/x/ URLs, e.g., Fc1bBw)

contentType.description: Type of content: page or blog post

contentFormat.description: Content format for page/comment body. Use "html" to write or read Confluence content as structured HTML. HTML supports standard blocks plus Confluence HTML+ data-type nodes: panels, status, task/decision lists, expands, layouts, cards, media, dates, mentions, macros/extensions, and sync blocks. HTML is round-trip safe and preserves inline comments and existing local IDs. It must follow valid ADF nesting rules: inline-only task/decision items, headings, and captions; no self-nesting panels, expands, tables, or blockquotes. Invalid HTML will be rejected with a descriptive error so you can retry. Use "markdown" for simplified plain text. Defaults vary by tool when omitted.

issueIdOrKey.description: Issue ID or key (e.g., PROJ-123 or 10000)

fields.description: Issue fields to return. When omitted or empty, defaults to: summary, description, status, issuetype, priority, labels, components, assignee, reporter, created, updated, resolution, project. Pass "*all" to return every field (including custom fields). Include "comment" to fetch issue comments in fields.comment.comments.

fieldsByKeys.description: Whether fields in the request are referenced by field keys instead of IDs.

expand.description: Additional issue details to expand in the response (for example, renderedFields or names).

properties.description: Issue property keys to include in the response.

updateHistory.description: Whether to update the user's recently viewed projects/history for this issue request.

failFast.description: Whether to fail quickly when some fields cannot be loaded instead of partially returning data.

responseContentFormat.description: Content format for body content. Use "markdown" for simplified plain text. Use "adf" (Atlassian Document Format, JSON) for full programmatic fidelity. Defaults vary by tool when omitted.

cql.description: CQL (Confluence Query Language) query string. CQL is specific to Confluence and is not JQL. Common fields: title, text, space, type, creator, contributor, label, ancestor, parent, lastmodified, created, mention, watcher, space.title, space.key. Use space key (not name) for the space field; use space.title ~ "name" for name search. Content types: page, blogpost, comment, attachment. Escape inner quotes with backslash: title ~ "Q2 \"planning\" review". Examples: title ~ "meeting notes" AND type = page | space.title ~ "Engineering" AND lastmodified >= now("-2w") AND type = page | creator = currentUser() AND type = page | text ~ "Q2 \"planning\" review" AND type = page

## 3. External product context

### [PROPOSED / PRD] Linked Confluence PRD

The linked page **PRD: QP <-> AI Toolkit Quest Skill** is current Confluence version 3, last modified 2026-09-18, and explicitly says `Draft, requirements only`.

Source: [PRD: QP <-> AI Toolkit Quest Skill](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QP/pages/25181847663/PRD+QP+-+AI+Toolkit+Quest+Skill)

The PRD user stories are:

- create a quest through natural language;
- list quests;
- view a specific quest;
- edit a quest;
- ask for missing required details rather than guessing;
- authenticate with Quest Platform without visible setup;
- specify a Web3 reward that is issued on completion.

The PRD also states that publisher/project scoping is a dependency, Web3 items must exist in a catalog, and the catalog location and item-creation flow are not defined. Its open questions include silent-authentication mechanics, quest deletion, and the minimum required quest fields.

Source sections: PRD sections `2. Summary`, `3. Requirements / User Stories`, `4. Dependencies`, and `5. Open Questions`.

### [PROPOSED / PRD] Parent reward direction

The parent **Token as Core Reward Engine** PRD describes tokens, NFTs, and collectibles, idempotent issuance, reconciliation, Backpack integration, AI Toolkit quest support, and a demo across surfaces. It is marked `In progress`, with dependencies and risks still listed.

Source: [PRD: Token as Core Reward Engine (In progress)](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QP/pages/25174540441/PRD+Token+as+Core+Reward+Engine+In+progress), sections `2. Background & Context`, `4. Scope`, `5. Non-Functional Requirements`, and `6. Known Dependencies & Risks`.

### [PROPOSED / JIRA] Story and reward dependencies

- [QP-2815: Quests in the AI Toolkit](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/QP-2815) is assigned to Rauf Aliyev, status `In progress`, updated 2026-09-18. Its description references viewing, creating, and editing quest flows, a headless Web Shop and in-product quests, NFT collections/tokens, the AI-kit repository, and the linked PRD.
- [QP-2814: Expanded Reward Modul](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/QP-2814) is assigned to Eljan Mahmudov, status `To Do`, updated 2026-09-18. Its description calls for ERC-20 and ERC-1155 support, idempotency, and reconciliation.
- [QP-2823: Token, NFT and collectibles rewards in Quests across surfaces](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/QP-2823) is assigned to Isidora Dukić, status `In progress`, updated 2026-09-17. Its description explicitly says visual prototype only, with no live Quest Platform integration and no real quest data.

Jira status is project coordination evidence, not proof that the implementation exists.

## 4. Meeting evidence

Source: `/Users/raufaliyev/Downloads/AI toolkit sync - 2026_09_18 12_30 CEST - Transcript.md`

### [MEETING] Narrowed first-demo scope

- The group discussed focusing AI Toolkit work on creating/managing quests and Web3 rewards, while leaving the Web Shop for a later version (`Transcript.md:41-59`).
- The proposed October 1 demonstration is terminal interaction with the AI toolkit, manual event firing, and seeing the resulting item in Backpack, with no visual web-shop requirement (`Transcript.md:49-59,181-205`).
- The demo is expected to show the quest creation flow first, then the event execution and Backpack result (`Transcript.md:191-211`).
- The admin panel is not expected to show Web3 reward analytics; Backpack is the visible result (`Transcript.md:211-219`).

### [MEETING] Missing-field and authoring behavior

- The desired user experience is natural language for a first-time Quest Platform user, with the agent asking questions about duration, audience, trigger/condition/reward details, and other missing information (`Transcript.md:77-87,129-139`).
- The discussion referenced following the conversational flow demonstrated by the Quest Platform CLI, but it was explicitly framed as something to check, not as a confirmed AI-kit dependency (`Transcript.md:111-123,223`).

## 1. Document Information

| Field | Details |
| --- | --- |
| **Feature Name** | Quest Platform AI Skill, v1 requirements |
| **Parent Epic** | [QP-2812 - Token as Core Reward Engine](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/QP-2812) |
| **Related Story** | [QP-2815 - Quests in the AI Toolkit](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/QP-2815) |
| **Status** | Draft, requirements only |

## 2. Summary

Publishers building with AI coding agents should be able to create, view, list, and edit quests through natural conversation, with the agent asking for anything it's missing rather than guessing. Authentication with Quest Platform should be invisible to the user. Publisher and project scoping is handled by a separate task and is a dependency here, not something this PRD defines. For v1, the only reward type in scope is web3 rewards.

## 3. Requirements / User Stories

| # | User Story | Acceptance Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | As a publisher user, I want to create a quest through my AI agent. | User can describe a quest in plain language and have it created. |
| 2 | As a publisher user, I want to list my quests through my AI agent. | User can ask to see their quests and get a list back. |
| 3 | As a publisher user, I want to view the details of a specific quest through my AI agent. | User can ask about a specific quest and see its full configuration. |
| 4 | As a publisher user, I want to edit an existing quest through my AI agent. | User can describe a change to an existing quest and have it applied. |
| 5 | As a publisher user, I want the agent to ask me for missing details when creating or editing a quest. | If required information is missing (for example, how long the quest should run, or what reward to give), the agent asks about it rather than guessing or failing silently. |
| 6 | As a publisher user, I want the skill to authenticate with Quest Platform without me having to set anything up. | No setup step, key entry, or visible credential step is required from the user; authentication happens automatically. |
| 7 | As a publisher user, I want to issue a web3 reward when a quest is completed. | User can specify a web3 reward when creating or editing a quest, and the reward is issued when the quest completes. |

## 4. Dependencies

| # | Dependency | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Publisher / project scoping | This skill needs to operate within a specific publisher and project. That scoping mechanism is defined in a separate task; this PRD assumes it exists and is available to the skill. |
| 2 | Web3 item catalog | Web3 rewards must exist somewhere before they can be issued through a quest. Where that catalog lives and how items get into it is not yet defined. |
| 3 | Web3 reward types in QP |  |

## 5. Open Questions

1. Where do web3 reward items come from, is there an existing catalog or registry of issuable web3 items, and if not, who owns creating one?
2. What form does the "silent authentication" take, is it a credential the skill obtains on first use, one pre-provisioned per publisher/project, or something else, and who is responsible for that mechanism?
3. Is quest deletion in scope for v1?
4. What counts as "required information" for a quest (Story 5) beyond duration and reward, is there an agreed minimal set of fields a quest must have?
"
}

content.text:
**1. По PRD это не нужно?** Формально да, это не требуется. В PRD и в QP-2890 есть только CRUD, недостающие поля и Web3-награда.

**2. Что я думаю?** Что нужно. Создать квест, отправить событие и ничего не знать о результате — это не норма. Как минимум скилл должен уметь ответить «квест выполнился / упал с такой-то ошибкой / ещё не сработал». Особенно с Web3: там ошибки видны только в рантайме. PRD написан как черновик требований, и этот сценарий там просто не продуман. Предложу добавить его как story 8.

**3. Почему именно `quest-executions`?** Тут я выразился неточно. Он не единственный, просто мы с ним работали в E2E. Он отдаёт статус выполнения, `eventId` для корреляции и статус с `error` по каждой action-ноде. Этого достаточно, чтобы ответить на вопрос из п.2.

**4. Почему не хватает `ledger/sessions`?** По форме ответа его, скорее всего, **хватает**. Я перепроверил модель ([ledger.go:30](lib/models/generic_quest/ledger.go:30)):
- фильтры `event_id`, `quest_id`, `user_id`, `quest_status`;
- в ответе `quest_status` и `executed_nodes`, где у каждой ноды есть `execution_status` и `execution_result`;
- авторизация — ключ аккаунта (`X-REQUEST-APIKEY`, проверяется через qp-server);
- маршрут публичный и на prod, и на stage.

Моё сомнение касается только **источника данных**, а не формата:
- `ledger/sessions` отдаёт quest-engine из **своей** БД (`offerwall`).
- В E2E мы видели выполнение в ledger **qp-worker-generic-quest**, а у него отдельная БД. Недаром quest-engine в `/quests/info` ходит за данными именно в ledger воркера.
- При этом quest-engine тоже читает топик `generic-quest-events` на stage и prod. Возможно, он тоже исполняет квесты и пишет свой ledger. По коду однозначно не понять, кто из двух исполняет наши квесты и пишет ли quest-engine туда что-то для них.

Это проверяется одним запросом по нашему тестовому квесту на stage. Ключ у тебя:

```bash
curl -s -H "X-REQUEST-APIKEY: $QP_API_KEY" "https://quests-stage.xsolla.com/api/v1/ledger/sessions?quest_id=2965a600-4f47-491c-aae7-60d0861b2caa&page_size=5"
```

- **Если там наши сессии** со статусом `COMPLETED` и нодой `issue_reward`, то verification переписывается на `ledger/sessions`. Это публичный хост, ключ аккаунта, внутренние сервисы не нужны, и слой можно публиковать сразу.
- **Если пусто**, то наши квесты исполняет только воркер. Тогда просим открыть наружу `/api/v1/quests/info`: он читает ledger воркера и принимает тот же ключ.

---
name: qp-publisher-auth-phases
description: "QP publisher machine lane (Basic merchant_id:api_key) is QP-2858 Phase 3, not started; only X-REQUEST-APIKEY works as of 2026-09-21"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4da9d811-791a-48d8-b4c4-17f8dfcbd956
  modified: 2026-09-22T05:34:59.436Z
---

The QP "Publisher access MVP" replaced the older framing of Farid's auth ADR
(Confluence 25179685430) as a single Proposed decision. As of 2026-09-21 it is a
three-phase Jira plan in project QP, and **nothing from it is merged into
`origin/dev`** (adtech's default branch is `dev`, there is no `main`).

- **Phase 1** QP-2851, service_identities / machine identity groundwork. In progress.
  Subtasks QP-2843..QP-2850. Farid Mammadov. Open stacked MRs !5491, !5493, !5494,
  !5495, !5496, each targeting the previous branch, none targeting `dev`.
- **Phase 2** QP-2852, second human issuer (Xsolla Publisher Account alongside Xsolla
  ID). To Do. Mirzakhan Aliyev. Open MR !5477 whose target `tech/QP-2852_auth-restructure`
  is already merged to `dev`, so the target is stale.
- **Phase 3** QP-2858, Xsolla scope mapping and the publisher machine lane. To Do,
  unassigned. Subtasks QP-2859..QP-2863. **QP-2862 is the `Authorization: Basic
  base64(merchant_ID:api_key)` lane.** Explicitly depends on Phase 1 and Phase 2.

Until QP-2862 lands, `MerchantKeyVerifier` in `qp-server/internal/auth/authenticate.go`
is a stub that always returns 401 "Merchant API key authentication is not yet
supported", and on `dev` the `Basic` scheme is not recognised at all. **The only
machine credential is `X-REQUEST-APIKEY` carrying a QP-internal UUID** bound to an
active row in `api_keys`. There is no token exchange anywhere in `qp-server/internal`.

Two Phase 3 rules that constrain any client built against QP:

- **Uniform 404.** Unknown, un-onboarded and unauthorized projects return byte-identical
  404s on purpose, because Xsolla project ids are a dense enumerable range and a
  403/404 split would leak QP's customer list. A 404 must never be reported as "it does
  not exist".
- **`ID 0` is a valid merchant id and a valid project id** and must never be treated as
  an absence sentinel.

Stacks 1 and 2 currently conflict: no branch contains both `Principal.Source`
(Mirzakhan) and `Principal.Owner{Kind,ID}` (Farid); they are competing reshapes of the
same struct, and Farid's deletes `HomeAcct`.
