content.text:
Вот что удалось проверить без ключа: только GET-запросы, ничего не пишется.

| Путь | stage | prod | Вывод |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/api/v1/ledger/sessions` | 401 `X-REQUEST-APIKEY header is required` | то же | ✅ публичный, это quest-engine |
| `/api/v2/quests` | 401 `Authentication required` | то же | ✅ публичный, это qp-server, **и на stage тоже** |
| `/api/v2/events` | 405 на GET | то же | ✅ маршрут есть (принимает только POST), это collector |
| `/api/v1/quests/info` | 404 `Cannot GET` | то же | ❌ ушёл в catch-all |
| `/api/v1/quest-executions`, `/quests/data/v1/...` | 404 `Cannot GET` | то же | ❌ qp-data наружу не открыт ни под каким путём |

Хорошая новость: на stage публично доступен и `/api/v2/quests`, а не только ledger, как было в твоей заметке. Значит, всю основную часть скилла можно тестировать через `quests-stage.xsolla.com`, без `*.srv.local`.

**Главный вопрос я закрыть не смог.** Что лежит в `ledger/sessions`, без ключа не узнать. А ключа нет ни в окружении, ни в памяти, и искать его по файлам я не стал. По коду тоже однозначного ответа нет:
- quest-engine и воркер читают один топик `generic-quest-events` (у них разные consumer group), и quest-engine тоже стартует generic-quest workflow;
- при этом в коде quest-engine я не нашёл ни одной записи в его таблицу `ledgers`, кроме админской.

Моя гипотеза: исполняет воркер, а ledger у quest-engine устаревший. Тогда `ledger/sessions` вернёт пустой ответ или старые данные. Но это гипотеза.

Чтобы закрыть вопрос, нужен один запрос с ключом. Экспортируй ключ в своём терминале и запусти:

```bash
curl -s -H "X-REQUEST-APIKEY: $QP_API_KEY" "https://quests-stage.xsolla.com/api/v1/ledger/sessions?quest_id=2965a600-4f47-491c-aae7-60d0861b2caa&page_size=5"
```

Если увидишь сессии с `issue_reward`, verification переносим на `ledger/sessions`. Если пусто, пишем владельцам: открыть `/api/v1/quests/info` в ingress.

```sql
SELECT k.key, k.name, k.role
FROM api_keys k
WHERE k.account_id = (SELECT account_id FROM quest_config WHERE id = '2965a600-4f47-491c-aae7-60d0861b2caa')

```

```bash
export QP_API_KEY=<key из запроса>
```

Если в `api_keys` у этого аккаунта несколько активных ключей, бери тот, у которого `role = 'service'`: им квест и создавали.

С master-ключом `ledger/sessions` по умолчанию смотрит в master-аккаунт, а в чужой аккаунт — только через параметр `account_id`. Партнёрский взгляд такой запрос не покажет, но на вопрос «есть ли вообще данные в ledger quest-engine» ответит.
- **Они теперь лежат в истории чата.** Я бы деактивировал лишние `test`-ключи и ротировал `Master API Key` на stage. Отдельно напомню ротировать и пароль БД из прошлого handoff'а.

Сделай так во вкладке `ledger check`:

```bash
export QP_API_KEY=<любой из master-ключей>
```

#!/bin/sh
# Read-only: GET quest -> account_id -> GET ledger/sessions. Never prints the key.
set -u
: "${QP_API_KEY:?set QP_API_KEY first}"
H=https://quests-stage.xsolla.com
Q=2965a600-4f47-491c-aae7-60d0861b2caa

echo "== GET /api/v2/quests/$Q"
quest=$(curl -s -m 15 -H "X-REQUEST-APIKEY: $QP_API_KEY" "$H/api/v2/quests/$Q")
echo "$quest" | jq -c '{id, name, status, account_id, publisher_id, project_id}' 2>/dev/null || echo "$quest" | head -c 500
acc=$(echo "$quest" | jq -r '.account_id // empty' 2>/dev/null)

for extra in "" "&account_id=$acc"; do
  echo
  echo "== GET /api/v1/ledger/sessions?quest_id=$Q$extra"
  curl -s -m 15 -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' -H "X-REQUEST-APIKEY: $QP_API_KEY" \
    "$H/api/v1/ledger/sessions?quest_id=$Q&page_size=5$extra" \
    | head -c 3000
done

content.text:
**Что проверяем.** Один вопрос: видны ли в публичном `ledger/sessions` исполнения наших квестов.

- Если видны, у скилла сразу появляется публичная проверка статуса. Тогда слой verification переписывается с внутреннего qp-data на `quests-platform.xsolla.com/api/v1/ledger/sessions` и публикуется вместе со всем стеком.
- Если не видны, публичной проверки статуса сейчас нет вообще. Verification ждёт, пока владельцы откроют маршрут (например `/api/v1/quests/info`).

**Если пропустим.** Ничего не сломается, просто решение по verification останется открытым. Тогда делаем так:
- публикуем то, что есть в PRD: groundwork, skeleton, quest-document, conditions, rewards. Это 5 PR, после чистки внутренних деталей;
- events и verification держим локально;
- владельцам QP задаём один вопрос: «какой публичный эндпоинт отдаёт статус исполнения квеста по `event_id` для ключа аккаунта?». Их ответ надёжнее нашего разового эксперимента на stage, который к тому же 20 минут назад лежал.

Я бы пропустил проверку и шёл дальше по этому пути. Эксперимент отвечает на вопрос, который нам всё равно придётся подтвердить у владельцев, а публикацию v1 он не блокирует.

Если согласен, следующий шаг — локальная чистка 5 слоёв. Я покажу тебе список замен до переписывания истории. И остаются два решения за тобой:
1. чистить ли внутренние детали в auth-секциях (`X-REQUEST-APIKEY`, stub, Jira-ключи) или оставить это Фариду;
2. схлопнуть ли каждый слой в один чистый коммит (старые ветки сохраню как `backup/*`).

Судя по коммиту `QP-2181: add qp-worker-generic-quest service` (2026-05-01), исполнение переехало в отдельный сервис, а в quest-engine остались только старт workflow и мёртвый код.
4. Значит, ledger пишет только воркер, в свою БД `qp_worker_generic_quest`. А публичный `ledger/sessions` отдаёт quest-engine из таблицы `ledgers` в БД `offerwall`, куда с мая никто не пишет. В лучшем случае там старые данные, но наших квестов там не будет.

| Эндпоинт | Данные актуальные? | Снаружи? | Ключ аккаунта? |
|---|---|---|---|
| quest-engine `/api/v1/ledger/sessions` | ❌ legacy-таблица | ✅ | ✅ |

**Вывод:** публичного способа проверить статус квеста сейчас нет. Меньше всего работы потребует открыть `/api/v1/quests/info` в ingress `quests-platform.xsolla.com`. content.text:
Нужен ответ на один вопрос паблишера: **«событие, которое я отправил, запустило мой квест, и награда выдалась?»**

Для этого с эндпоинта нужно четыре вещи:

| Данные | Зачем |
|---|---|
| **`event_id`** (фильтр или поле в ответе) | убедиться, что смотрим результат **именно нашего** события, а не старого успешного выполнения того же квеста у того же пользователя |
| **статус квеста**: `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `NOT_TRIGGERED` (или «ещё идёт») | сказать паблишеру «сработал / упал / не сработал». `NOT_TRIGGERED` значит, что событие не подошло: имя не совпало с триггером, квест неактивен, лимит исчерпан, условие не прошло |
| **статус каждой action-ноды** (прежде всего `issue_reward`) | квест может в целом завершиться, а конкретная награда нет. Паблишера интересует именно награда |
| **текст ошибки ноды** | объяснить, что починить. Например, Web3-награда упала из-за неправильной суммы или SKU: qp-server такие ошибки при создании не ловит, они видны только здесь |

Плюс одна вещь для безопасности. Если нода висит в «выполняется» или упала по таймауту, скилл **не должен переотправлять событие**, потому что выплата могла уже пройти. Без статуса агент этого не знает и может выплатить дважды.

Больше ничего не нужно: ни метрики, ни история, ни тело события. Всё это `/api/v1/quests/info` уже отдаёт. Фильтр `event_id`, статус квеста и `executed_nodes` со статусом и результатом по каждой ноде есть в его ответе. Поэтому я и предлагаю попросить открыть наружу именно его.

content.text:
Сейчас скилл сам не заработает после работы Фарида. Я сверил скилл с планом авторизации (QP-2862 в Jira) и с кодом collector'а и нашёл три блокера:

**1. Маршруты поменяются.** В QP-2862 прямо написано:
> Require `project_id` from the route. A Basic credential on a route without it is unresolvable by construction — reject

А скилл сейчас намеренно работает через **scopeless**-маршруты `/api/v2/quests` («scope приходит из креденшала»). С project API key такие запросы будут отклоняться. Нужны маршруты с `project_id` в пути, их обещает QP-2860 («may add project-scoped publisher-facing routes»). Точной формы пути пока нет.

**2. Collector project API key не примет.** `qp-events-collector` проверяет только `X-REQUEST-APIKEY` ([middleware.go:87](qp-events-collector/internal/http/middleware/middleware.go:87)). Ни одна из auth-веток (QP-2851, 2852, 2853) collector не трогает. CRUD квестов заработает, а отправка события нет.

**3. OpenAPI на проде закрыт.** Скилл берёт маршруты и форму запросов из live `/openapi.json`, а на prod qp-server эти пути блокирует. Для внешнего агента правило «Source of truth» не работает.

**Как сделать, чтобы скилл заработал без правок:**
- Auth-секцию переписать на **целевой** контракт: `Authorization: Basic base64(merchant_id:api_key)`, стандартные для кита `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` и `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY` (как в `catalog-design` и `merchant-setup`). Без «not accepted yet», stub'ов и Jira-ключей. 401 трактовать нейтрально: «ключ не принят для этого проекта».
- Маршруты описать в той форме, которую выберет Фарид. Лучше всего попросить его **открыть `/openapi.json` на prod**. Тогда скилл находит маршруты сам и подстроится под любую финальную форму. Это решает и п.1, и п.3.
- События: либо collector получает тот же Basic lane, либо в v1 отправка событий остаётся за паблишером (с его бэкенда). Скилл просто объясняет формат.

**Вопросы Фариду** (могу набросать сообщение):
1. Какая будет форма project-scoped маршрутов, `/api/v2/projects/{project_id}/quests`?
2. Можно ли открыть `/openapi.json` на prod?
3. Входит ли collector (`/api/v2/events`) в Basic lane, и когда?

Пока ответов нет, я бы стек **не публиковал**. Иначе в публичном репо окажется скилл, который не работает ни сейчас, ни после релиза Фарида. Чистку внутренних деталей при этом могу сделать уже сейчас, локально. Делаем так?

  ````markdown
  # Authentication and environment
  
  This is the **only** file that names the host, the header and the credential.
  Everywhere else says "an authenticated Quest Platform request". Keep it that
  way, so a change to authentication touches one file.
  
  ## Host
  
  Every request, quest configuration and event submission alike, goes to:
  
  ```
  https://quests-platform.xsolla.com
  ```
  
  There is no environment variable for the host. Do not send requests to any
  other host, and do not switch hosts after an error.
  
  ## Credential
  
  ```bash
  export XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
  export XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
  export XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
  ```
  
  Every request sends
  `Authorization: Basic base64(XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID:XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY)`, the
  same pattern other skills in this kit use.
  
  Use the key on the server or agent side only. Never print it, never write it
  into a file the developer will share, and never send it to a browser. When
  you confirm the variables are set, show the key as `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=****`.
  
  ## Routes
  
  | Operation | Route |
  |---|---|
  | List quests | `GET /api/v2/quests` |
  | Create a quest | `POST /api/v2/quests` |
  | Read a quest | `GET /api/v2/quests/{id}` |
  | Replace a quest | `PUT /api/v2/quests/{id}` |
  | Submit an event | `POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events` |
  
  `project_id` in the event route is `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`.
  
  ## Checking access
  
  Project API key access to Quest Platform is rolling out one operation at a
  time. Listing quests at bring-up shows whether the key works for reads. Treat
  each new operation the same way when it first returns an error:
  
  - **404 with a plain-text body** such as `Cannot GET /api/v2/quests` or
    `Cannot POST /api/v2/quests`: the route is not published on this host yet.
    Stop. Tell the developer that project API key access for this operation is
    not available yet. Do not retry, and do not try another host or credential.
  - **401 with a JSON body**: the host received the credential and did not
    accept it for this project. Ask the developer to check `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID`
    and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY`.
  - **404 with a JSON body**: not found, no access, or the project is not
    onboarded to Quest Platform. These cases look identical by design. Never say
    the quest or the project does not exist.
  
  ## Scope
  
  The quest routes take no account or project in the path. The scope comes from
  the credential. Before the first write, list quests and show the developer the
  `account_id`, `publisher_id` and `project_id` that come back, then ask them to
  confirm that is the right place. If the list is empty, show
  `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` instead and ask the same
  question. Do not guess a scope, and do not silently accept whichever scope the
  credential happens to carry.
  ````

  ````markdown
  # Events

  as quest configuration; see [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md).
  
  `POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events`
  
  `project_id` is `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`. The project is taken from the path, so
  the body names no publisher, project or account.
  
  ## Payload
  
  ```json
  {
    "idempotency_key": "<uuid>",
    "name": "<event_name from the trigger>",
    "client_timestamp": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "user_ids": [{"identifier_type": "xsolla_id", "value": "<uuid>"}],
    "quest_id": "<uuid>",
    "scope": "private",
    "properties": {"any": "string values only"}
  }
  ```
  
  | Field | Required | Rules |
  |---|---|---|
  | `idempotency_key` | yes | a valid, non-zero UUID. Any UUID version is accepted |
  | `name` | yes | must match the `event_name` on the quest's `dynamic_event` trigger |
  | `client_timestamp` | yes | RFC3339 |
  | `user_ids` | yes | at least one entry |
  | `quest_id` | no | a valid UUID when present |
  | `scope` | no | `global`, `private`, `within_project`, `within_quest`, `within_publisher`. Defaults to `private` |
  | `properties` | no | string values only |
  
  `user_ids[].identifier_type` is `xsolla_id`, `gamer_id`, `guest_id` or `email`.
  An `xsolla_id` value must parse as a UUID; an `email` value must contain `@`;
  `gamer_id` and `guest_id` need only be non-empty.

  whose user already has a wallet. Confirm it with the developer before
  submitting; see [`rewards.md`](rewards.md).
  
  ## Idempotency
  
  There are two separate mechanisms and they are easy to confuse:
  
  - the body field `idempotency_key`, which identifies the event
  - a generic HTTP `X-Idempotency-Key` header, which must be exactly 36
    characters
  
  Use the body field. Generate a fresh UUID per event.

  "event accepted, `event_id=<id>`". Then say that this skill cannot yet read
  back whether the quest executed, and that the developer should check the
  outcome where the reward lands. Never claim a reward was delivered.

  resend, not with the same key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
  failure: the event may have been accepted and the quest may already be paying
  out. Report "result unknown".

  is not an uncertain response. It means event submission is not available for
  project API keys yet; see [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md).
  ````

````markdown
# Authentication and environment

This is the **only** file that names the host, the header and the credential.
Everywhere else says "an authenticated Quest Platform request". Keep it that
way, so a change to authentication touches one file.

## Host

Every request, quest configuration and event submission alike, goes to:

```
https://quests-platform.xsolla.com
```

There is no environment variable for the host. Do not send requests to any
other host, and do not switch hosts after an error.

## Credential

```bash
export XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
export XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
export XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
```

Every request sends
`Authorization: Basic base64(XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID:XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY)`, the
same pattern other skills in this kit use.

Use the key on the server or agent side only. Never print it, never write it
into a file the developer will share, and never send it to a browser. When
you confirm the variables are set, show the key as `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=****`.

## Routes

| Operation | Route |
|---|---|
| List quests | `GET /api/v2/quests` |
| Create a quest | `POST /api/v2/quests` |
| Read a quest | `GET /api/v2/quests/{id}` |
| Replace a quest | `PUT /api/v2/quests/{id}` |
| Submit an event | `POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events` |

`project_id` in the event route is `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`.

## Checking access

Project API key access to Quest Platform is rolling out one operation at a
time. Listing quests at bring-up shows whether the key works for reads. Treat
each new operation the same way when it first returns an error:

- **404 with a plain-text body** such as `Cannot GET /api/v2/quests` or
  `Cannot POST /api/v2/quests`: the route is not published on this host yet.
  Stop. Tell the developer that project API key access for this operation is
  not available yet. Do not retry, and do not try another host or credential.
- **401 with a JSON body**: the host received the credential and did not
  accept it for this project. Ask the developer to check `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID`
  and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY`.
- **404 with a JSON body**: not found, no access, or the project is not
  onboarded to Quest Platform. These cases look identical by design. Never say
  the quest or the project does not exist.

## Scope

The quest routes take no account or project in the path. The scope comes from
the credential. Before the first write, list quests and show the developer the
`account_id`, `publisher_id` and `project_id` that come back, then ask them to
confirm that is the right place. If the list is empty, show
`XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` instead and ask the same
question. Do not guess a scope, and do not silently accept whichever scope the
credential happens to carry.
````

````markdown
# Events

Events go to the events endpoint on the same host, with the same credential
as quest configuration; see [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md).

`POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events`

`project_id` is `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID`. The project is taken from the path, so
the body names no publisher, project or account.

## Payload

```json
{
  "idempotency_key": "<uuid>",
  "name": "<event_name from the trigger>",
  "client_timestamp": "2026-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "user_ids": [{"identifier_type": "xsolla_id", "value": "<uuid>"}],
  "quest_id": "<uuid>",
  "scope": "private",
  "properties": {"any": "string values only"}
}
```

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `idempotency_key` | yes | a valid, non-zero UUID. Any UUID version is accepted |
| `name` | yes | must match the `event_name` on the quest's `dynamic_event` trigger |
| `client_timestamp` | yes | RFC3339 |
| `user_ids` | yes | at least one entry |
| `quest_id` | no | a valid UUID when present |
| `scope` | no | `global`, `private`, `within_project`, `within_quest`, `within_publisher`. Defaults to `private` |
| `properties` | no | string values only |

`user_ids[].identifier_type` is `xsolla_id`, `gamer_id`, `guest_id` or `email`.
An `xsolla_id` value must parse as a UUID; an `email` value must contain `@`;
`gamer_id` and `guest_id` need only be non-empty.

A quest with a `web3_item` or `web3_token` reward needs an `xsolla_id` entry
whose user already has a wallet. Confirm it with the developer before
submitting; see [`rewards.md`](rewards.md).

## Idempotency

There are two separate mechanisms and they are easy to confuse:

- the body field `idempotency_key`, which identifies the event
- a generic HTTP `X-Idempotency-Key` header, which must be exactly 36
  characters

Use the body field. Generate a fresh UUID per event.

## After a 200

A 200 returns `{"idempotency_key": "...", "event_id": "<uuid>"}`. Report
"event accepted, `event_id=<id>`". Then say that this skill cannot yet read
back whether the quest executed, and that the developer should check the
outcome where the reward lands. Never claim a reward was delivered.

## After an uncertain response

If the request times out or the outcome is otherwise unknown, **stop**. Do not
resend, not with the same key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
failure: the event may have been accepted and the quest may already be paying
out. Report "result unknown".

A 404 with a plain-text body such as `Cannot POST /api/v2/projects/<id>/events`
is not an uncertain response. It means event submission is not available for
project API keys yet; see [`auth-and-environment.md`](auth-and-environment.md).
````

## Decisions beyond your instructions
- **Routes table.** With OpenAPI no longer a source, the references have to list the routes. I added a table to `auth-and-environment.md`, taken from the local qp-server handler comments. It covers list, create, read and replace on the scopeless `/api/v2/quests` routes, plus the events route.

- **Empty quest list at scope confirmation.** If the list comes back empty, the skill shows `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID` and asks the developer to confirm them. The original text had no answer for this case.
- **Reward-retry safety stop.** The old stops relied on reading back a `FAILED` action, which is now out of scope. I replaced them with two:

  - "never resend an event to retry a Web3 reward"

So I rewrote the row and its paragraph to say: with neither `items` nor `item_sku`, the platform picks a random item and the skill tells the developer first. I also added "each `items[].sku` required; quantity 0 means 1". This replaces the vague "an empty body can mean a runtime-selected item".

  - The event timestamp example is now `2026-01-15T10:30:00Z`.

- **Whole-token amounts.** I don't know whether fractional amounts like `0.5` are accepted. The text says "whole-token amount greater than 0" and doesn't address fractions.

- **Plain-text 404 across reads and writes.** I assumed a plain-text 404 means the same thing for every operation, and wrote the access check per operation.

name: quest-setup
description: >-
  Creates, inspects, edits and activates Xsolla Quest Platform quests
  conversationally, and submits a quest event to make a quest run. Covers the
  whole quest document: the node graph and its connections, all seven node
  subtypes, the condition grammar, activation limits, and all nine reward types

  quest, adding a trigger or a condition, attaching a reward, editing or
  activating an existing quest, or firing a test event, including "create a
  quest", "add a Web3 reward to my quest", "make a quest that pays USDC",

## Status

This skill is a **draft**. It requires project API key access to Quest
Platform, which is rolling out. See Errors for how an unavailable route looks.

## When to use

Use this skill when the developer wants to manage quests on the Xsolla Quest
Platform:

- Create a quest, as a draft first and then activate it
- Add triggers, conditions or reward actions to a quest
- List, view or edit existing quests
- Submit a single quest event to make a quest run

Out of scope: reading back whether a quest executed, on-chain finality, wallet
balances and Backpack display. This skill configures quests and submits
events. It reports that an event was accepted and never states that a reward
was delivered.

## Prerequisites

Follow [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md)
for the host, the credential and scope confirmation. The credential is the
project API key. Use it on the server or agent side only.

## Source of truth

1. This skill's `references/` are the contract: routes, fields, node
   subtypes, node `parameters`, the condition grammar, reward bodies and
   enums.
2. If a live response contradicts them, trust the shape of the live response,
   tell the developer what differed, and do not guess the rest.
3. If neither answers the question, **ask the developer**. Do not infer a
   field by analogy with another Xsolla API.

## Reference material

- [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md): host, credential, routes, access check and scope
- [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md): the quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT
- [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md): the seven accepted node subtypes and their parameters
- [`references/conditions.md`](references/conditions.md): condition grammar: types, operands, operators, event counting
- [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): the nine reward types and their bodies, including Web3 rewards
- [`references/events.md`](references/events.md): submitting a quest event

## Flow

1. **Bring-up.** Check the credential is set. List quests, show the scope that
   comes back, and get confirmation.
2. **Draft.** Create the quest as `inactive` with the four required fields.
3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
   required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
   there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
   nodes, and an acyclic graph.
   For a Web3 reward, also run the checks in
   [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount and the
   recipient's wallet, all confirmed with the developer.
   Show the activation limits and the effective repeat behavior before asking
   for confirmation.
5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
   document.
6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
   an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit it to
   the events endpoint.
7. **Report.** On success, report "event accepted, `event_id=<id>`". Say that
   this skill cannot yet read back whether the quest executed, and that the
   developer should check the outcome where the reward lands. Never claim a
   reward was delivered.

## Safety stops

- Show the resolved scope before the first write, and get confirmation.
- Before activation, show every externally observable action and get explicit
  confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;
  `send_http_webhook` sends event data to an external URL;
  `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user notification. Do not activate a
  `webshop_personalization` node as if it were a working personalization action.
- If `activation_limits` is absent, ask the developer to explicitly choose
  unlimited repeat behavior and acknowledge that every qualifying event may run
  the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.
- Ask for confirmation before submitting an event.
- After an uncertain event response, such as a timeout, **do not resend**:
  not with the same idempotency key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
  failure. Report "result unknown" and stop.
- If the developer reports that a reward did not arrive, do not resend the
  event to retry it. Fix the quest first, then send a new event with a new key
  only after the developer confirms.
- Never resend an event to retry a Web3 reward. The Web3 claim is not
  idempotent and may already have paid; see
  [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
- Never claim a reward was delivered.

## Errors

Branch on the HTTP status. The only body check is on a 404: a plain-text body
and a JSON body mean different things. The API has no stable machine-readable
error codes.

| Status | What to tell the developer |
|---|---|
| 401, JSON body | The credential was not accepted for this project. Ask the developer to check `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY`. |
| 403 | The key lacks permission for quest configuration. |
| 404, plain-text body such as `Cannot GET /...` or `Cannot POST /...` | The route is not published on this host yet. Stop and tell the developer that project API key access for this operation is not available yet. Do not retry and do not try other hosts. |
| 404, JSON body | "Not found, or no access, or the project is not onboarded to Quest Platform." Never say the quest does not exist. |
| 409 | Conflict. |
| 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. |
| 5xx | Server error. Retry reads only. |

A JSON 404 looks the same for an unknown project, a project that is not
onboarded, and a project the key has no access to. This is deliberate, so the
API cannot be used to find out which projects use Quest Platform.

Two JSON body shapes exist. Failures before the request reaches a quest
operation, such as authentication, return `{"error": "..."}`. Failures inside
the operation return RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. On 422 the `errors[]` array is
**not** filled in: per-field messages are flattened into one `detail` string
joined with `"; "`. Those `location: message` pairs may be shown to a human,
never parsed for control flow.

`ID 0` is a valid merchant ID and a valid project ID. Never treat it as an
absent value.

   subtypes, node `parameters`, the condition grammar, reward bodies and
   enums.
2. If a live response contradicts them, trust the shape of the live response,
   tell the developer what differed, and do not guess the rest.
3. If neither answers the question, **ask the developer**. Do not infer a
   field by analogy with another Xsolla API.

## Reference material

- [`references/auth-and-environment.md`](references/auth-and-environment.md): host, credential, routes, access check and scope
- [`references/quest-document.md`](references/quest-document.md): the quest graph, conditional requirements, full-document PUT
- [`references/node-subtypes.md`](references/node-subtypes.md): the seven accepted node subtypes and their parameters
- [`references/conditions.md`](references/conditions.md): condition grammar: types, operands, operators, event counting
- [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): the nine reward types and their bodies, including Web3 rewards
- [`references/events.md`](references/events.md): submitting a quest event

## Flow

1. **Bring-up.** Check the credential is set. List quests, show the scope that
   comes back, and get confirmation.
2. **Draft.** Create the quest as `inactive` with the four required fields.
3. **Fill in.** Add nodes and edges one at a time, asking for each missing
   required value. Show the assembled document before sending it.
4. **Activate.** A separate step: move to `active` with dates, after checking
   there are at least two nodes, a trigger-to-action path, no intended orphan
   nodes, and an acyclic graph.
   For a Web3 reward, also run the checks in
   [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md): SKU, amount and the
   recipient's wallet, all confirmed with the developer.
   Show the activation limits and the effective repeat behavior before asking
   for confirmation.
5. **Edit.** Read, change, full `PUT`. Warn that `PUT` replaces the whole
   document.
6. **Event.** Build the payload, generate a fresh UUID `idempotency_key`, set
   an RFC3339 `client_timestamp`, confirm with the developer, and submit it to
   the events endpoint.
7. **Report.** On success, report "event accepted, `event_id=<id>`". Say that
   this skill cannot yet read back whether the quest executed, and that the
   developer should check the outcome where the reward lands. Never claim a
   reward was delivered.

## Safety stops

- Show the resolved scope before the first write, and get confirmation.
- Before activation, show every externally observable action and get explicit
  confirmation for its impact. An `issue_reward` can create real payouts;
  `send_http_webhook` sends event data to an external URL;
  `send_xsolla_app_notification` sends a user notification. Do not activate a
  `webshop_personalization` node as if it were a working personalization action.
- If `activation_limits` is absent, ask the developer to explicitly choose
  unlimited repeat behavior and acknowledge that every qualifying event may run
  the action. Do not silently choose a limit or omit this decision.
- Ask for confirmation before submitting an event.
- After an uncertain event response, such as a timeout, **do not resend**:
  not with the same idempotency key and not with a new one. A timeout is not a
  failure. Report "result unknown" and stop.
- If the developer reports that a reward did not arrive, do not resend the
  event to retry it. Fix the quest first, then send a new event with a new key
  only after the developer confirms.
- Never resend an event to retry a Web3 reward. The Web3 claim is not
  idempotent and may already have paid; see
  [`references/rewards.md`](references/rewards.md).
- Never claim a reward was delivered.

## Errors

Branch on the HTTP status. The only body check is on a 404: a plain-text body
and a JSON body mean different things. The API has no stable machine-readable
error codes.

| Status | What to tell the developer |
|---|---|
| 401, JSON body | The credential was not accepted for this project. Ask the developer to check `XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID` and `XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY`. |
| 403 | The key lacks permission for quest configuration. |
| 404, plain-text body such as `Cannot GET /...` or `Cannot POST /...` | The route is not published on this host yet. Stop and tell the developer that project API key access for this operation is not available yet. Do not retry and do not try other hosts. |
| 404, JSON body | "Not found, or no access, or the project is not onboarded to Quest Platform." Never say the quest does not exist. |
| 409 | Conflict. |
| 422 | Validation failed. Show `detail` verbatim. |
| 5xx | Server error. Retry reads only. |

A JSON 404 looks the same for an unknown project, a project that is not
onboarded, and a project the key has no access to. This is deliberate, so the
API cannot be used to find out which projects use Quest Platform.

Two JSON body shapes exist. Failures before the request reaches a quest
operation, such as authentication, return `{"error": "..."}`. Failures inside
the operation return RFC 7807 `application/problem+json`. On 422 the `errors[]` array is
**not** filled in: per-field messages are flattened into one `detail` string
joined with `"; "`. Those `location: message` pairs may be shown to a human,
never parsed for control flow.

`ID 0` is a valid merchant ID and a valid project ID. Never treat it as an
absent value.

# Rewards

These are the `parameters` of a node with `type: action` and
`subtype: issue_reward`.

## Wrapper

```json
{"type": "<reward type>", "purpose": "<string>", "body": { }}
```

`type`, `purpose` and a non-empty `body` are all required. An unrecognised
`type` is rejected.

## Bodies

| `type` | `body` | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `xsolla_points` | `{"amount": <number>}` plus optional `campaign_name`, `campaign_image`, `event_name`, `reason_quest_id`, `app_name`, `app_icon_url` | `amount` greater than 0 |
| `virtual_currency` | `{"amount": <number>}` | `amount` greater than 0 |
| `loyalty_points` | `{"amount": <number>, "loyalty_points_id": "<string>"}` | both required |
| `lootbox` | `{"item_sku": "<string>", "quantity": <int>}` | `quantity` 1 to 100 |
| `custom` | `{"amount": <number>, "currency_ticker": "<string>"}` | `amount` greater than 0 |
| `inventory_item` | `{"xsolla_item": <bool>, "items": [{"sku": "<string>", "quantity": <int>, "type": "<string>", "name": "<string>", "image_url": "<url>", "model_3d_url": "<url>"}], "item_sku": "<string>", "name": "<string>", "image_url": "<url>", "model_3d_url": "<url>"}` | `items` or `item_sku`; each `items[].sku` required; item quantity 0 to 100, treated as 1 when 0 or absent. With neither, a random item, see below |
| `vc_wallet_ticket` | `{"quantity": <int>, "currency_ticker": "<string>"}` plus optional `playtime` | `quantity` greater than 0 |
| `web3_item` | `{"xsolla_item": <bool>, "item_sku": <string or array>, "quantity": <int>}` | `quantity` at least 0, treated as 1 when absent. No `item_sku` means a random item, see below |
| `web3_token` | `{"item_sku": "<token SKU>", "amount": <number>}` | both required; `amount` is a whole-token amount greater than 0, see below |

The optional `playtime` object on `vc_wallet_ticket` is
`{"earn_rate_minutes": <greater than 0>, "daily_cap_minutes": <greater than 0>, "timezone": "<non-empty>"}`.

For `inventory_item`, provide either `items` or the single-item `item_sku`
form. `name`, `image_url` and `model_3d_url` go with the single-item form.
Obtain real catalog values from the developer. A body with neither `items` nor
`item_sku` makes the platform pick a random item; tell the developer before
choosing that. Acceptance never proves that a particular SKU exists.

## Web3 rewards

`web3_item` and `web3_token` pay to the wallet of the event's user.

### Recipient

The event's `user_ids` must include an `xsolla_id`, and that user must already
have a wallet. This skill cannot check that. Confirm it with the developer
before activation and again before submitting an event. If the user has no
wallet, the payout fails.

### Mistakes surface at payout time

The Quest API does not check a Web3 body against the payout provider. It
accepts an unknown SKU or a wrong amount on create, `PUT` and activation alike.
Such a mistake fails only when the reward is paid out. Confirm the SKU and the
amount with the developer before activation.

### web3_item

An NFT from the developer's Web3 catalog. Take the SKU from the developer's
Web3 catalog or from Xsolla. Never invent one.

Omitting `item_sku` makes the platform pick a random item. Tell the developer
before choosing that.

### web3_token

An ERC-20 payout, for example USDC.

```json
{
  "type": "web3_token",
  "purpose": "quest_completion",
  "body": {"item_sku": "<token SKU>", "amount": 5}
}
```

- `item_sku` is the token SKU from the developer's Web3 catalog or from
  Xsolla. Never invent one.
- `amount` is a whole-token amount and must be greater than 0: `5` pays 5
  tokens.
- Show the token SKU and the amount back to the developer and get them
  confirmed before activation.

### No retries

The Web3 claim is not idempotent. Never resend an event to retry a Web3
reward. After an uncertain response, stop: the payout may already have
happened. Never claim that a token or an item reached a wallet.

### Activation

Attaching a Web3 reward to a quest that you then activate means real payouts.
Ask for explicit confirmation before activating.

Create or update a stack on GitHub from branch names, PR numbers, or PR URLs.

This command does not rely on gh-stack local tracking state. It is
designed for users who manage branches with external tools (e.g. jj,
Sapling, ghstack, git-town, etc...) and want to use GitHub stacked
PRs without adopting local stack tracking.

Arguments are provided in stack order (bottom to top). Each argument
can be a branch name, a PR number, or a PR URL (e.g.
https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123). For numeric arguments, the
command first checks if a PR with that number exists; if not, it
treats the argument as a branch name. PR URLs are always resolved
as pull requests (never as branch names).

Branch arguments are automatically pushed to the remote before
creating or looking up PRs. For branches that already have open PRs,
those PRs are used. For branches without PRs, new PRs are created
automatically with the correct base branch chaining.

If the PRs are not yet in a stack, a new stack is created. If some of
the PRs are already in a stack, the existing stack is updated to include
the new PRs (existing PRs are never removed).

As a shortcut for growing an existing stack, pass a stack number as the
first argument (the number shown in the GitHub stack UI). The remaining
arguments are appended to the top of that stack, so you don't have to
re-list its current PRs. Arguments already in the stack are skipped;
arguments that belong to a different stack are rejected. Because stack and
PR numbers never overlap, a numeric first argument is treated as a stack
only when it matches an existing stack.

Usage:
  gh stack link <stack-number | branch-or-pr> <branch-or-pr> [<branch-or-pr>...] [flags]

Examples:
  # Link branches into a stack (bottom to top)
  $ gh stack link auth-layer api-routes ui-components

  # Link existing PRs by number
  $ gh stack link 41 42 43
[]

| # | PR |
|---|---|
| 1 | [#38](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/38) QP-2888: validator and guide groundwork for the quest skill |
| 2 | [#39](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/39) QP-2890: quest-setup skill skeleton, registries and auth |
| 3 | [#40](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/40) QP-2890: quest document and node subtypes |
| 4 | [#41](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/41) QP-2890: condition grammar |
| 5 | [#42](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/42) QP-2890: reward bodies, including Web3 |
| 6 | [#43](https://github.com/xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit/pull/43) QP-2890: event submission |

**Что вошло:**
- **Auth переписан на целевой контракт:** `Basic base64(XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID:XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY)`, хост `quests-platform.xsolla.com`. Всё про авторизацию лежит в одном файле.
- **Обходные пути:**
  - **Маршрут ещё не опубликован.** Пока доступа по project API key нет, сервер отвечает на такие маршруты 404 с текстом вида `Cannot GET /...`. Скилл понимает это как «ещё не опубликовано», честно говорит об этом и не перебирает другие хосты.
  - **События.** Идут на `POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events` из ADR Фарида, с тем же ключом.
  - **Источник правды.** Вместо закрытого OpenAPI им стали `references/`.
- **Verification убран.** Скилл сообщает «event accepted, `event_id`» и не утверждает, что награда дошла.
- **Коммиты.** По одному чистому коммиту на слой.
- **Проверки.** Grep по внутренним паттернам (хосты, сервисы, minting, id, Jira, stage) по всем коммитам и их сообщениям дал 0 совпадений. Валидатор проходит на каждом слое, зеркало `.cursor` совпадает.

**Локально:**
- Все 7 старых веток сохранены как `backup/*`.
- Слой verification остался только в `QP-2890-verification`, он не запушен.
- Твои незакоммиченные файлы не тронуты.

**Что осталось открытым:**
1. **Фарид.** Для запросов по project API key проект, похоже, должен быть в пути (QP-2862), а скилл пока ходит на `/api/v2/quests` без проекта. Если это так, правка будет только в `auth-and-environment.md`. Это вынесено в «Open questions» в #39.
2. **Ingress.** `/api/v2/projects/*` сейчас наружу не маршрутизируется. После релиза Фарида нужен маршрут в terraform, иначе события будут отвечать `Cannot POST`.

4. **Ключи.** 15 master-ключей stage теперь лежат в истории чата. Я бы деактивировал `test`-ключи и ротировал `Master API Key`, а заодно пароль БД из прошлого handoff'а.

content.text:
Да, главный блокер — авторизация Фарида. Но она не единственная, и часть пунктов можно двигать параллельно.

## Что осталось по скиллу

**Ждём других:**
1. **Фарид, project API key (QP-2862).** Зависит от Phase 1 и 2, сейчас в статусе To Do и без исполнителя. Без него скилл не может сделать ни одного запроса.
2. **Фарид, форма маршрутов.** Нужно подтвердить, будут ли CRUD-запросы с Basic работать на `/api/v2/quests` или проект должен быть в пути. Во втором случае нужна правка одного файла.
3. **Фарид, события.** Эндпоинт `POST /api/v2/projects/{project_id}/events` в collector'е (ADR 5.1) пока не реализован.
4. **Ingress.** `/api/v2/projects/*` не маршрутизируется наружу. Это отдельная строчка в terraform, её легко забыть.

**Можем сделать сами:**
5. **Agent test.** Когда появится доступ, прогнать и записать результат в SKILL.md. Без этого `CONTRIBUTING-skills.md` не пускает PR в мёрж.
6. **Ревью.** Перевести PR из draft и отдать на ревью. Финальное ревью и мёрж делает @j.manashti. Можно отдать уже сейчас, чтобы замечания по тексту пришли до релиза auth.
7. **Jira:**
   - QP-2890 до сих пор To Do;
   - описание QP-2888 не совпадает с содержимым;
   - в QP-2898 нет записи о сегодняшнем E2E.
8. **Потом.** Verification: предложить story 8 в PRD и попросить открыть `/api/v1/quests/info` снаружи.

## Web3 reward

**Что работает.** Сегодня на stage прошёл полный E2E: событие принято, `issue_reward` дошёл до COMPLETED, перевод USDC подтверждён on-chain.

**Проблемы, которые нужно передать Web3-команде (Eljan):**

| Проблема | Почему важно |
|---|---|
| **Единицы суммы.** Контракт (`issue_reward.go`) говорит «whole tokens», а воркер передаёт `amount` как есть, и minting принимает только целые base units | Скилл написан по контракту: `5` означает 5 токенов. На текущем stage `5` выплатит 5 base units, то есть 0.000005 USDC, а `0.5` упадёт с 400. Это баг воркера, до фикса скилл даёт неверный результат |
| **Prod-конфиг.** `WEB3_ERC20_PROJECT` на prod пустой | `web3_token` на проде сейчас всегда падает. Команда в курсе, говоришь, что доведёт до прода |
| **Один ERC-20 проект на весь воркер** | Все паблишеры платят токенами одного проекта. Непонятно, как паблишер получит свой токен или SKU |
| **`web3_item` только из дефолтного каталога.** Воркер не передаёт проект | NFT паблишера из его каталога сейчас выдать нельзя |
| **Claim без идемпотентности.** Таймаут или ретрай activity могут привести к двойной выплате | Скилл это обходит правилом «никогда не переотправлять», но на платформе риск остаётся |
| **Claim на stage, похоже, без авторизации.** Инцидент с 1 USDC сегодня утром | Потенциальная дыра, если на prod так же |
| **Кошелёк.** Нет публичного способа проверить, есть ли кошелёк у пользователя | Скилл только просит паблишера подтвердить |

Самое срочное здесь — **баг с единицами суммы**. От него зависит, правильно ли работает то, что уже в PR.

Подготовить сообщение Eljan по этим пунктам, без адресов кошельков и tx hash, и отдельное короткое Фариду по пунктам 2–4?

# xsolla-ai-kit — Agent Context

This file is read automatically by most AI coding agents (Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Amp, Devin, Jules, Aider, Roo Code, Augment). Claude Code users: `CLAUDE.md` is a copy of this file.

---

## What this repo is

`xsolla/xsolla-ai-kit` is the Xsolla agent skills toolkit — a collection of `SKILL.md` files (agentskills.io format) that teach AI coding agents how to execute Xsolla-specific workflows end-to-end, without requiring the Xsolla CLI as a dependency.

Skills call **Xsolla REST APIs directly**. The CLI (`xsolla/xsolla-cli`) is an optional shortcut once it ships to production.

---

## Skill inventory

| Skill                           | What it does                                                                             |
|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `shop-setup`                    | **Orchestrator** — coordinates the full zero-to-shop flow, chaining all domain skills    |
| `merchant-setup`                | Creates and configures an Xsolla account + get API key                                   |
| `catalog-design`                | Configures the catalog and the client flow: client catalog, purchase, order confirmation |
| `login-setup`                   | Integrates Xsolla Login / NewID authentication                                           |
| `login-styling`                 | Applies a custom visual style / theme / brand to the Login UI (pairs with `login-setup`) |
| `headless-checkout-integration` | Payments via Headless Checkout                                                           |
| `webhooks-impl`                 | Generates webhook handler code for order/payment events                                  |
| `quest-setup`                   | Creates and manages Quest Platform quests, events and rewards                            |
| `production`                    | Sandbox → live: contract, flip flags, deploy, developer live-payment checklist           |

---

## How to invoke a skill

Skills are loaded automatically when you open this repo in your agent. To run a specific skill, ask your agent naturally:

```
Set up a full Xsolla game shop for my project
→ triggers: shop-setup

Configure my Xsolla catalog with items and pricing
→ triggers: catalog-design

Integrate payments into my game
→ triggers: headless-checkout-integration

Go live / leave sandbox
→ triggers: production

Create a quest that rewards players
→ triggers: quest-setup
```

---

## Environment variables

```bash
XSOLLA_MERCHANT_ID=<your merchant ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_ID=<your project ID>
XSOLLA_PROJECT_API_KEY=<your API key>
```
Setup by `merchant-setup` skill.

---

## Key directories

| Path | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `skills/` | SKILL.md files. One subdirectory per workflow. |
| `skills/<name>/references/` | Long-form reference docs. Keeps SKILL.md under 200 lines. |
| `docs/` | Architecture, distribution, and skill-gap guides. |
| `.cursor/skills/` | Cursor-native skills (synced copy of `skills/`; do not edit manually) |
| `.cursor/rules/` | Short always-on Cursor pointer rule |

---

## Adding a skill

See [CONTRIBUTING-skills.md](CONTRIBUTING-skills.md) for the full guide.

Quick rules:
- One `SKILL.md` per `skills/<skill-name>/` directory
- Under 200 lines; split into `references/` if it grows past that
- Description must contain trigger keywords — make it pushy
- No `curl` commands — skills describe intent, not raw HTTP
- PR must include agent test output (exact prompt + one-line result)

{
  "id": "24953094441",
  "type": "page",
  "status": "current",
  "title": "Web3 NFT Reward via Quest Platform — Integration Guide",
  "spaceId": "22283420592",
  "parentId": "24615452798",
  "parentType": "folder",
  "authorId": "712020:d3605aa9-bf85-445a-8a7d-ffdc574d43e6",
  "ownerId": "712020:d3605aa9-bf85-445a-8a7d-ffdc574d43e6",
  "lastOwnerId": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-08-05T05:17:51.606Z",
  "version": {
    "number": 5,
    "message": "",
    "minorEdit": false,
    "authorId": "712020:d3605aa9-bf85-445a-8a7d-ffdc574d43e6",
    "createdAt": "2026-09-15T10:36:52.116Z",
    "ncsStepVersion": "42"
  },
  "body": "> **Audience:** Quest Platform team, Offerwall team **Status:** Verified end to end on stage — [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9), [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9), and a SKU from a second IGS project **Service:** `web3-minting-service` (repo `solidity/node/xsolla-zk-tokens-binding-api`)
> 
> **Stage instance: **`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local`
> 
> **Prod instance: **`https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local`

---

## 1. What this gives you

A quest can now mint a **real NFT on XsollaZK** as its reward. Quest Platform does not need to know anything about blockchains: it fires its usual `send_http_webhook` action node, and the minting service resolves the player's wallet, submits the on-chain claim, and records who got what.

Two token standards are covered:

| Reward | How it is requested | What the player gets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) (unique item) | `properties.amount` omitted, or `"1"` | 1 unique token, fresh id |
| [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) (fungible stack) | `properties.amount` \> 1 | N units of one shared id |

Gas is paid by the platform. The player needs no external wallet — the tokens land in their Xsolla Backpack (thirdweb Ecosystem Wallet).

An item is addressed by **project id + SKU**, not by SKU alone: a SKU is only unique inside its IGS project, and two projects may both ship `sword_01`.

---

## 2. High-level flow

```
  Client backend            qp-events-collector        quest-engine            web3-minting-service         XsollaZK
  ──────────────            ───────────────────        ────────────            ────────────────────         ────────
        │                            │                      │                          │                      │
        │── POST /api/v2/events ────▶│                      │                          │                      │
        │   (idempotency_key,        │── Kafka ────────────▶│                          │                      │
        │    name, quest_id,         │                      │ resolve quest            │                      │
        │    user_ids[xsolla_id],    │                      │ walk the graph           │                      │
        │    properties: sku,        │                      │── POST /quest-reward ───▶│                      │
        │    project, amount)        │                      │                          │                      │
        │                            │                      │                          │ resolve wallet       │
        │◀───────── 200 OK ──────────│                      │◀──── 202 Accepted ───────│ from xsolla_id       │
        │                            │                      │                          │                      │
        │                            │                      │                          │── claim(...) ──────▶│
        │                            │                      │                          │◀── tokenId ─────────│
        │                            │                      │                          │ write minted_instances
```

Everything after the `202` is asynchronous. The `202` is deliberate — see §6.

---

## 3. Endpoints

All internal (`.srv.local`) — Xsolla VPN required.

| Service | Stage |
| --- | --- |
| Stage Minting service | `https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local` |
| Prod Minting service | `https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-prod.srv.local` |
| Quest management (qp-server) | `https://qp-server.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` |
| Event collector (qp-events-collector) | `https://qp-events-collector.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local` |

Interactive API docs: `https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/docs`

Public read-only routes (`/metadata`, `/image`, `/skus`) send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` so they can be fetched from a browser on another origin. The state-changing routes deliberately do not.

---

## 4. Step 1 — the quest

The reward is a `send_http_webhook` action node pointing at the minting service. Nothing web3-specific goes in the quest config.

```json
{
  "id": "<node-uuid>",
  "name": "Mint NFT via Web3 Minting Service",
  "type": "action",
  "subtype": "send_http_webhook",
  "type_version": "1.0",
  "parameters": {
    "url": "https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/quest-reward"
  }
}
```

`quest-demo.sh` in the repo builds the whole quest, fires the event, and reads back the mint, if you want a working reference:

```
export QP_API_KEY=<uuid>
./quest-demo.sh create-quest
./quest-demo.sh fire-event --quest-id <uuid> --xsolla-id <uuid> \
  --sku lootbox_0 --igs-project 44056 --amount 10
./quest-demo.sh status --idempotency-key <uuid>
```

### Put the mint node in parallel, not in series

If a quest also grants a Backpack `inventory_item`, connect **both** actions directly to the trigger rather than chaining them:

```
"connections": {
  "<trigger-id>": [{ "nodeId": "<mint-hook-id>" }, { "nodeId": "<inventory-item-id>" }],
  "<mint-hook-id>": [],
  "<inventory-item-id>": []
}
```

Chained, a failing `inventory_item` node stops the mint from ever running. We hit exactly this on stage: the Backpack grant fails for a publisher/project with no catalog item, and in series it took the mint down with it.

---

## 5. Step 2 — the event

Standard `POST /api/v2/events`. Two fields matter for the mint:

```
curl -X POST https://qp-events-collector.nl-k8s-stage.srv.local/api/v2/events \
  -H 'X-REQUEST-APIKEY: <your-api-key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "idempotency_key": "055f6d06-2a1c-4d0c-b651-c2b90b406c31",
    "name": "web3.quest_completed",
    "scope": "global",
    "quest_id": "0a1a71b5-9b33-4f77-ac7d-13b5d41309a1",
    "user_ids": [
      { "identifier_type": "xsolla_id", "value": "0cf3cd1d-c86b-4621-b22c-7d65af91dcea" }
    ],
    "client_timestamp": "2026-08-04T08:39:00Z",
    "properties": {
      "sku": "lootbox_0",
      "project": "44056",
      "amount": "10"
    }
  }'
```

### `user_ids` must carry `xsolla_id`

The recipient wallet is resolved from it. **Quest Platform does not derive this** — the client sends it. No other identifier type works: `email`, `gamer_id` and `guest_id` cannot be resolved to a wallet. Without it the hook answers `422`.

The wallet itself *is* automatic: the service looks up `user_wallet_mapping` first, then thirdweb by the same id, preferring the [EIP-4337](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/EIP-4337?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) smart account. No pre-registration is required for a player who already has a Backpack wallet.

### `properties` — what to mint

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sku` | yes, unless the service has a default configured | IGS item to mint |
| `project` | no | IGS project the SKU belongs to. Defaults to the project the service is configured for. |
| `amount` | no | Quantity. Omitted or `"1"` ⇒ [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9). Greater ⇒ [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9). Positive integer, string or number. |

Note the boundary: **a single unit of an **[**ERC-1155**](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9)** cannot be requested.** `amount: "1"` always mints an [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9), because the standard is inferred from the quantity.

**Send **`project`** whenever the item is not in the service's default project.** The SKU is not validated against the catalogue before minting, so a SKU that does not exist in the project being used still mints — and produces a token whose metadata never resolves. To check a pair before using it:

```
curl 'https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/skus?project=312479&search=00222'
```

### What the hook ignores

Everything else — `scope`, `publisher`, `account_id`, `server_timestamp` and any other property — is accepted and ignored. Quest Platform owns the payload shape, so unknown fields are never rejected.

Deliberately **not** readable from the payload: the recipient address and the NFT collection. Those come from service configuration. A hook that any in-cluster caller can reach must not be able to name its own wallet or contract.

---

## 6. Why the hook answers `202`, and what that means for you

A `202` means *accepted*, not *minted*. The claim runs in the background.

This is not laziness: an on-chain claim regularly takes longer than Quest Engine's 30s webhook timeout, and Quest Engine retries three times. Acknowledging only after the mint would guarantee a timeout, a retry, and a second mint of the same reward. We measured the retry behaviour on stage — three POSTs 1–3s apart per delivery — while the endpoint was still returning 404.

Consequences worth knowing:

- `202`** does not mean the player has the token yet.** Typical settle time is a few seconds; the ceiling is the claim timeout (120s).
- **Retries are safe.** A redelivered `idempotency_key` returns `200` with the original record and mints nothing.
- **A quest showing **`COMPLETED`** does not prove the mint succeeded.** `COMPLETED` means the webhook returned 2xx. Check the mint separately, below.

### Reading the outcome

```
curl https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/quest-reward/055f6d06-2a1c-4d0c-b651-c2b90b406c31
```

```json
{
  "idempotencyKey": "055f6d06-2a1c-4d0c-b651-c2b90b406c31",
  "status": "minted",
  "user": "0cf3cd1d-c86b-4621-b22c-7d65af91dcea",
  "projectId": "44056",
  "sku": "lootbox_0",
  "amount": "10",
  "tokenStandard": "erc1155",
  "toAddress": "0x517D8742682207ba0922bf982E20669B6c864a7d",
  "recipientSource": "thirdweb:smart",
  "contractAddress": "0xE7e9050bA4A2a1a61eD5274acFaB10c07300Afaa",
  "txHash": "0x3b8149dc5a649bcefcec1e55e3a90c2bbbed316f86cae089f1d28eb3882c434b",
  "tokenId": "17",
  "error": null
}
```

`status` is `pending` → `minted` / `failed`. On failure, `error` carries the reason.

These records live in memory, so they are lost on restart and capped at the most recent 10 000 deliveries. For durable state, use `/minted-instances` below.

---

## 7. For Offerwall — what a player owns

```
curl https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/minted-instances/0cf3cd1d-c86b-4621-b22c-7d65af91dcea
```

```json
{
  "user": "0cf3cd1d-c86b-4621-b22c-7d65af91dcea",
  "walletAddress": "0x517d8742682207ba0922bf982e20669b6c864a7d",
  "recipientSource": "thirdweb:smart",
  "total": 2,
  "instances": [
    {
      "projectId": "44056",
      "sku": "lootbox_0",
      "collectionAddress": "0xe7e9050ba4a2a1a61ed5274acfab10c07300afaa",
      "tokenId": "18",
      "tokenStandard": "erc1155",
      "amount": "10",
      "txHash": "0x3b8149dc…",
      "mintedAt": "2026-08-04T08:41:02.000Z"
    },
    {
      "projectId": "44056",
      "sku": "lootbox_0",
      "collectionAddress": "0x9389fee265b30281728e5c7a00a654f05036cfe9",
      "tokenId": "14",
      "tokenStandard": "erc721",
      "amount": "1",
      "txHash": "0x3b58f934…",
      "mintedAt": "2026-08-04T08:29:20.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

Path parameter is the **Xsolla user id** — same identifier as everywhere else, resolved to a wallet server-side.

This is backed by the `minted_instances` table, written after every successful claim. Two properties to design around:

- **A row says a wallet holds a token, not how many.** `amount` is the quantity of the claim that *created* the row. A repeat [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) claim of the same id does not increment it. **For a true balance, read the chain** (`balanceOf(address, id)`).

  Measured on stage: two `amount: "10"` claims of `lootbox_0` minted 10 units each (tx `0x11b2e6f2…` then `0xd462f843…`), so the wallet holds **20** on chain — while the table still shows one row with `amount: "10"` and the first tx hash. Do not present this field as a balance.
- **Uniqueness is **`(wallet_address, collection_address, token_id)`**.** Token ids are only unique within a collection, so the same number in two collections is two different tokens. The row also carries `project_id`, because `sku` alone does not identify an item.

Mint state is **not** written back to IGS. It lives on our side, in this table.

---

## 8. Verified on stage

| Case | Event | tokenId | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) | `amount` omitted | 13 on `0x9389…CfE9` | quest `COMPLETED`, `status: minted`, tx `0x3b58f934…` |
| [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) | `amount: "10"` | 17 on `0xE7e9…Afaa` | quest `COMPLETED`, `status: minted`, tx `0x3b8149dc…`, `balanceOf = 10`, `totalSupply = 10` |
| Retry | same `idempotency_key` replayed | — | `200`, `duplicate: true`, no second mint |
| `minted_instances` write | [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) then [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) | 17 and 14 | two rows — one per collection, confirming the composite key |
| Repeat [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) | second `amount: "10"` of the same SKU | 17 reused | minted on chain (tx `0xd462f843…`), **no new row**, `amount` still `"10"` |
| Project-scoped | `amount: "10"`, `project: "44056"` | 18 on `0xE7e9…Afaa` | quest `COMPLETED`, `status: minted`, tx `0xb672c7b2…`, record carries `projectId: "44056"` |

Token ids differ between runs because each claim mints a new [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) id, while the [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) id is reused from the SKU's binding — that reuse is what makes repeat claims fungible.

Cross-cluster reachability is confirmed: quest-engine in `nl-k8s-stage` reaches the service in `gcp-k8s-web3-stage` (seen in the ingress log from `172.16.13.x`).

One caveat on verification: the public RPC (`579029.rpc.thirdweb.com`) load-balances across nodes with divergent state, so `balanceOf` at `latest` intermittently returns `0` for a token that exists. Pin a block number when checking balances, or read `totalSupply`.

---

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| Quest `COMPLETED`, no token | The webhook returned 2xx but the claim failed later. Read `GET /quest-reward/{idempotency_key}` — `status: failed` carries the reason. |
| `422 user_ids must contain an entry with identifier_type "xsolla_id"` | The event carried `email` / `gamer_id` only. Resolve to an Xsolla id before firing. |
| `404 no wallet found for user` | The player has no `user_wallet_mapping` row and no thirdweb wallet. Usually a player who has never opened their Backpack. |
| `400 sku is required` | No `properties.sku` and no default configured on the service. |
| `503 database is not configured` | [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) only — token-id reuse needs the database. [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) works without it. |
| `401 invalid webhook secret` | `QUEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set on the service; add `?secret=<value>` to the node URL. A webhook node sends no custom headers, so the query param is the only channel. |
| Got an [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) when expecting [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) | `amount` was `"1"`. Use a quantity greater than 1. |
| Minted, but the token's metadata does not resolve | The SKU does not exist in the project that was used. SKUs are not validated before minting. Check with `GET /skus?project=…&search=…`. |
| `400 project must be 1-64 chars…` | `properties.project` carried something outside letters, digits, `-` and `_`. It goes into an upstream URL path, so it is rejected rather than forwarded. |
| Updating a quest returns `422 start_date must be on or after …` | `PUT /api/v2/quests/{id}` takes the full body, and qp-server rejects a `start_date` in the past. Move it to today when editing. |
| Quest `FAILED` with a Backpack `inventory_item` node | That node fails independently of the mint (no catalog item for the publisher/project). Put the two actions in parallel — see §4. |

---

## 10. Creating the item — and what we need from you

The minting service does not create catalogue items. It reads them from IGS, so the item has to exist there first. Create it in Publisher Account, in the project you want it under, then send us **the project id and the SKU**. That pair is all we need.

Verify it is visible to us before handing it over — this reads the same catalogue the service does:

```
curl 'https://web3-minting-service.gcp-k8s-web3-stage.srv.local/skus?project=<PROJECT_ID>&search=<SKU>'
```

```json
{ "projectId": "312479", "count": 1, "items": [ { "sku": "00222", "name": "Test", "type": "virtual_good" } ] }
```

`count: 0` means we cannot see it — usually the wrong project id, or the item is not enabled for the catalogue. Nothing downstream will work until this returns your item, and it fails quietly: **the SKU is not validated at mint time**, so a wrong pair still mints a token, one whose metadata resolves to nothing.

The name, description and image the player sees come from this catalogue entry, live — the token's on-chain URI points back at us and we read IGS on every request. Fixing a typo in Publisher Account fixes it for tokens already minted; nothing has to be re-minted.

### Virtual currency

Virtual currency lives in the same catalogue, under its own type:

```
curl 'https://store.xsolla.com/api/v2/project/<PROJECT_ID>/items/virtual_currency?locale=en&country=US'
curl 'https://store.xsolla.com/api/v2/project/<PROJECT_ID>/items/virtual_currency/package?locale=en&country=US'
```

Project `44056` currently has two currencies (`crystal`, `gold`) and five packages; project `312479` has none.

**What we support today: virtual items only.** There is no support for currencies — not one, and certainly not an arbitrary number of them. A currency is not simply an item with a different label: the reward path infers [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) versus [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) from `amount`, reuses a token id per SKU, and writes one row per `(wallet, collection, token)`. A currency needs balance semantics — accumulate on repeat grants, and a real balance to read back — which that model does not provide, and which is the same gap already noted for `amount` in §7.

**What we can do:** wire up **one specific currency** by hand. If you create it and send us its project id and SKU, we can add the mapping for that single currency. It stays a one-off — every additional currency would be the same manual work again, so treat it as a demo path, not a feature.

If you need many currencies properly, say so and we will scope it as its own piece of work; it is a different data model, not a configuration change.

---

## 11. Open items

- `QUEST_WEBHOOK_SECRET`** is not yet provisioned.** Until it is sealed, the hook mints for any caller that can reach the pod from inside the cluster network. Fine for integration testing; it should be set before anything user-facing.
- **Backpack **`inventory_item`** rewards fail** for publisher `877754` / project `304175` — that project's catalogue is empty (`GET /skus?project=304175` returns nothing). Independent of the mint path, but it fails any quest that chains the two nodes.
- `amount`** does not accumulate** in `minted_instances` on repeat [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) claims. Say if you need a running total there rather than reading the chain.
- **Production has no database.** `DATABASE_URL` is unset there, so [ERC-1155](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-1155?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) claims, `/minted-instances` and the wallet-mapping routes are unavailable in prod. [ERC-721](https://xsolla.atlassian.net/browse/ERC-721?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiYjM0MTA4MzUyYTYxNDVkY2IwMzVjOGQ3ZWQ3NzMwM2QiLCJwIjoianN3LWdpdGxhYlNNLWludCJ9) mints work, resolving the recipient from thirdweb.
- **Production on-chain config still points at the same testnet contracts as stage.**
"
}

>
